strings.Fixed mode normally clamps the request t: Fixed mode normally clamps the request to the static safe estimate. This advanced option lets the private benchmark server try the exact fixed value above that estimate; a bounded allocation failure affects only that job and the suite continues.

strings.Chooses a smaller draft or assistant mod: Chooses a smaller draft or assistant model that may speed up generation by proposing tokens for the main model to verify.
strings.Lists external draft, EAGLE-3, DFlash, a: Lists external draft, EAGLE-3, DFlash, and supported embedded MTP paths. AutoTuner marks likely incompatibilities with ⚠ but keeps them selectable. Selecting a draft enables it immediately; selecting no draft disables model-based speculative decoding. The choice is remembered per model.
strings.Includes or excludes every saved folder: Includes or excludes every saved folder from scanning in one step.
strings.This toggles each list item's enabled st: This toggles each list item's enabled state without deleting its path. Only enabled roots are searched; pressing Cancel discards the dialog changes, while OK persists the resulting path/state pairs.
strings.Lists saved folders. Check a folder to s: Lists saved folders. Check a folder to scan it, or uncheck it to keep the path saved but temporarily ignore it.
strings.Paths are normalized and duplicate roots: Paths are normalized and duplicate roots are removed. Model folders are scanned recursively for GGUF files; llama-build roots are scanned for runnable platform-compatible server binaries.
strings.Adds another folder to this list and ena: Adds another folder to this list and enables it immediately.
strings.The selected directory is resolved to an: The selected directory is resolved to an absolute path, deduplicated against existing entries, and persisted only after OK is pressed.
strings.Replaces the selected entry with a diffe: Replaces the selected entry with a different folder.
strings.The replacement keeps the item's enabled: The replacement keeps the item's enabled state, stores a resolved absolute path, and removes any duplicate created by the change.
strings.Removes the selected folder from the sav: Removes the selected folder from the saved list.
strings.This removes only AutoTuner's path entry: This removes only AutoTuner's path entry; it never deletes the folder, models, llama.cpp build, or any files on disk.
strings.Previews and selects the application's c: Previews and selects the application's color and font theme.
strings.Built-ins stay read-only; edited built-i: Built-ins stay read-only; edited built-ins are saved as new '-user' themes, while selected user themes can be updated in the per-installation theme folder.
strings.Shows the running AutoTuner version and: Shows the running AutoTuner version and GitHub project page.
strings.The dialog is local and does not contact: The dialog is local and does not contact GitHub; use Update to check for newer source or release versions.
strings.Reloads JSON files copied into the user: Reloads JSON files copied into the user theme folder.
strings.Invalid files are ignored and listed in: Invalid files are ignored and listed in a warning; the selected valid theme is reapplied.
strings.Opens the selected theme in the safe col: Opens the selected theme in the safe color and font editor.
strings.Built-ins are copied to a draft with '-u: Built-ins are copied to a draft with '-user' appended to the ID and name; Save validates it. Saving an existing user theme with the same ID atomically updates it.
strings.Opens the folder used for your own theme: Opens the folder used for your own themes.
strings.Files in this persistent folder survive: Files in this persistent folder survive source updates and compiled-binary swaps; click Reload after copying a JSON file.
strings.Opens AutoTuner automatically after you: Opens AutoTuner automatically after you sign in, so it is ready without a manual launch.
strings.This creates a per-user startup entry on: This creates a per-user startup entry only; it does not install a service and needs no administrator rights. Windows uses HKCU Run, Linux an XDG autostart file, and macOS a user LaunchAgent. Turning the option off removes that entry.
strings.Records extra AutoTuner discovery and co: Records extra AutoTuner discovery and configuration details for support.
strings.This affects AutoTuner's own debug categ: This affects AutoTuner's own debug categories and rotating application log only. It does not enable llama-server --verbose, capture prompts or API payloads, or include credentials. A restart is not required.
strings.Lets trusted programs on this computer s: Lets trusted programs on this computer select and use your AutoTuner models through one stable OpenAI-compatible address.
strings.The gateway binds only to 127.0.0.1, req: The gateway binds only to 127.0.0.1, requires a cryptographically random bearer token, serializes model switches, reuses saved launch settings, and stops only the previous API-managed model.
strings.Chooses the local port used by external: Chooses the local port used by external clients.
strings.The listener is always loopback-only. Th: The listener is always loopback-only. The default is 1233 so it does not collide with llama-server's default base port 1234.
strings.The secret that authorised local clients: The secret that authorised local clients must send as a bearer token.
strings.It contains at least 256 bits of random: It contains at least 256 bits of random material and is stored in the per-user settings file. Regenerating it immediately invalidates old client configurations after you accept this dialog.
strings.Copies only the current API key to the c: Copies only the current API key to the clipboard.
strings.The clipboard contains a credential unti: The clipboard contains a credential until another application replaces it; paste it only into a trusted local client.
strings.Creates a new random API key in this dia: Creates a new random API key in this dialog.
strings.The old key remains active until OK is c: The old key remains active until OK is clicked. Environment-owned keys cannot be regenerated here.
strings.Copies the endpoint and key names used b: Copies the endpoint and key names used by AutoTuner's Pi extension.
strings.The two newline-separated environment as: The two newline-separated environment assignments are AUTOTUNER_API_URL and AUTOTUNER_API_KEY; the copied key is a secret.
strings.Saves measured tuning profiles to a port: Saves measured tuning profiles to a portable JSON backup.
strings.Exports validated Expert snapshots and b: Exports validated Expert snapshots and benchmark evidence for all four performance targets. Atomic writing prevents partial bundles.
strings.Restores performance profiles from an Au: Restores performance profiles from an AutoTuner JSON backup.
strings.Strictly validates the bundle schema, me: Strictly validates the bundle schema, merges valid target profiles, and maps local GGUFs by exact filename plus byte size.
strings.Adaptive mode prevents a large first mod: Adaptive mode prevents a large first model or Safe profile from forcing the same context onto a smaller model or Throughput profile.
strings.For every suite job AutoTuner recomputes: For every suite job AutoTuner recomputes placement, KV precision, runtime buffers, native/YaRN limits, and the safe context against the exact selected llama build and its detected backend.
strings.Quick pass is the default short search;: Quick pass is the default short search; Standard validates the 12.5% workload; Custom uses the exact percentage below.
strings.Quick pass uses at most 16,384 prompt to: Quick pass uses at most 16,384 prompt tokens and 128 decode tokens with no overall model/suite deadline. Startup and individual HTTP timeouts still detect stuck servers. Standard uses a 65,536 prompt cap. Custom values from 0.01% through 100% deliberately ignore it.
strings.Change one value while AutoTuner safely: Change one value while AutoTuner safely adjusts related values to keep the configuration practical for your hardware.
strings.Each edited field becomes a pinned overr: Each edited field becomes a pinned override and compute_config() re-runs around it. Context, KV-cache precision, memory placement, and other dependent values may change so the resulting VRAM/RAM plan still fits.
strings.Keeps every value exactly as you enter i: Keeps every value exactly as you enter it, without automatic safety adjustments.
strings.The panel assembles a TunedConfig direct: The panel assembles a TunedConfig directly from the widget values; compute_config() is not re-run. Invalid or overcommitted memory, thread, batch, or fork-specific combinations can therefore make llama-server slow down or fail to start.
strings.Removes this model's saved Expert change: Removes this model's saved Expert changes and returns to the fully automatic recommendation.
strings.The per-model Expert snapshot and pinned: The per-model Expert snapshot and pinned overrides are deleted, then compute_config() is run again from the current model metadata, hardware state, performance target, and launch options.
strings.Closes the Expert editor and returns to: Closes the Expert editor and returns to the normal configuration preview.
strings.This only changes the visible panel. Sav: This only changes the visible panel. Saved Expert overrides remain associated with the selected model until you use Reset; no server is started or stopped.
strings.Sets how much recent text, code, and con: Sets how much recent text, code, and conversation the model can consider at once. More context helps with large tasks but needs more memory.
strings.Passed as llama-server --ctx-size. KV-ca: Passed as llama-server --ctx-size. KV-cache memory grows roughly linearly with context length and with the number of parallel slots. In Auto mode, changing it triggers a new KV precision and CPU/GPU placement plan so the requested window fits when possible.
strings.Chooses the quality and memory use of th: Chooses the quality and memory use of the model's attention-key memory. Higher precision is safer for recall; lower precision saves VRAM or RAM.
strings.This maps to --cache-type-k. f16 uses th: This maps to --cache-type-k. f16 uses the most memory, q8_0 is a high-quality compromise, and q4/q5 or TurboQuant formats compress more aggressively. Flash Attention is required for quantized KV types on supported llama.cpp builds.
strings.Chooses the quality and memory use of th: Chooses the quality and memory use of the attention-value cache. Lower precision can free substantial memory for a longer context.
strings.This maps to --cache-type-v. With Flash: This maps to --cache-type-v. With Flash Attention, compatible AMD/Vulkan builds can use an asymmetric K/V plan, often keeping K at higher precision than V. Some backends or older builds require matching types and may reject unsupported combinations.
strings.Controls how much of a regular dense mod: Controls how much of a regular dense model runs on the GPU. More GPU layers are usually faster but consume more VRAM.
strings.Passed as --n-gpu-layers. 0 keeps layers: Passed as --n-gpu-layers. 0 keeps layers on CPU; 999 requests full offload and lets llama.cpp clamp to the model's actual layer count. Mixture-of-Experts placement is governed separately by n_cpu_moe.
strings.For Mixture-of-Experts models, moves exp: For Mixture-of-Experts models, moves expert layers to system RAM when VRAM is limited. More CPU expert layers save VRAM but are usually slower.
strings.Passed as --n-cpu-moe. It affects MoE ex: Passed as --n-cpu-moe. It affects MoE expert tensors rather than the dense shared layers controlled by --n-gpu-layers. 0 keeps eligible experts GPU-resident; larger values progressively offload them.
strings.Sets how many CPU threads generate token: Sets how many CPU threads generate tokens. AutoTuner normally picks a sensible value for your processor.
strings.Passed as --threads / -t for the token-g: Passed as --threads / -t for the token-generation phase. Too few threads can bottleneck CPU work; too many can increase scheduling, cache, and hybrid-core overhead without improving speed.
strings.Sets CPU parallelism while the initial p: Sets CPU parallelism while the initial prompt is processed. A good value can reduce time to the first generated token.
strings.Passed as --threads-batch / -tb. Prompt: Passed as --threads-batch / -tb. Prompt ingestion can use different parallelism from token generation; excessive threads may hurt on hybrid CPUs or when several servers share the machine.
strings.Controls how many prompt tokens llama.cp: Controls how many prompt tokens llama.cpp may prepare together. Larger batches can process prompts faster but need more temporary memory.
strings.Passed as --batch-size / -b. This is the: Passed as --batch-size / -b. This is the logical maximum batch and must be at least as large as the physical micro-batch. Very high values can increase compute-buffer VRAM/RAM or fail on constrained backends.
strings.Sets the smaller chunks actually sent th: Sets the smaller chunks actually sent through the model during prompt processing. Smaller chunks use less peak memory; larger chunks may be faster.
strings.Passed as --ubatch-size / -ub. llama.cpp: Passed as --ubatch-size / -ub. llama.cpp divides the logical batch into these physical micro-batches. It should not exceed batch size, and backend-specific memory limits often determine the best value.
strings.Allows several requests or agents to gen: Allows several requests or agents to generate at the same time. Leave it off unless you need concurrency, because every slot uses additional memory.
strings.Enables a manual --parallel / -np overri: Enables a manual --parallel / -np override. llama-server uses continuous batching and allocates a KV window per slot, so total KV memory scales with slot count. Off delegates the count to the chosen performance target (one slot by default).
strings.Chooses the exact number of simultaneous: Chooses the exact number of simultaneous request slots after the parallel override is enabled.
strings.Passed as --parallel N. Each slot receiv: Passed as --parallel N. Each slot receives its own context/KV-cache capacity, so raising N can reduce the context that fits or cause memory pressure. AutoTuner suggests 3 with at least 24 GiB free on the largest GPU and otherwise 2.
strings.Uses a faster, more memory-efficient att: Uses a faster, more memory-efficient attention implementation when the selected backend supports it.
strings.Passed as --flash-attn / -fa. It is requ: Passed as --flash-attn / -fa. It is required by llama.cpp for quantized KV-cache types and can reduce attention memory traffic. Unsupported GPU/backend combinations may ignore or reject it.
strings.Chooses whether model weights are mapped: Chooses whether model weights are mapped, read normally, locked in RAM, or loaded through direct I/O. Auto keeps llama.cpp's default.
strings.Passed as --load-mode MODE. Since b10151: Passed as --load-mode MODE. Since b10151, mlock means locking without mmap and mmap+mlock explicitly combines both. none disables mapping without locking; dio requests DirectIO when the platform supports it. Locking still requires sufficient RAM and OS privileges. AutoTuner blocks it on old or unprobeable GPU builds with the historic Vulkan host-buffer crash.
strings.Lets llama-server format messages using: Lets llama-server format messages using the chat template stored with the model, including supported reasoning output handling.
strings.Passed as --jinja. llama.cpp renders the: Passed as --jinja. llama.cpp renders the GGUF/Jinja template for the OpenAI-compatible chat API and can separate supported <think> traces into reasoning_content. A missing or broken template may require a different template override.
strings.Prints much more server detail for troub: Prints much more server detail for troubleshooting. Leave it off for a quieter terminal during normal use.
strings.Passed as --verbose. The llama-server te: Passed as --verbose. The llama-server terminal includes additional request, scheduler, model, and backend diagnostics; this can produce large logs and may expose prompt/request metadata during debugging.
strings.Adds a monitoring page that tools such a: Adds a monitoring page that tools such as Prometheus can read. It does not change model quality.
strings.Passed as --metrics and exposes GET /met: Passed as --metrics and exposes GET /metrics on the same server host and port. The endpoint reports operational counters and timings; if you bind beyond localhost, protect it with the same network controls as the inference API.
strings.Lets AutoTuner show how many request slo: Lets AutoTuner show how many request slots are busy or available. It is mainly useful when serving concurrent clients.
strings.Passed as --slots and enables llama-serv: Passed as --slots and enables llama-server's GET /slots endpoint. AutoTuner polls compatible builds for busy/total state. The endpoint can reveal runtime details, so avoid exposing it on an untrusted network.
strings.Controls how memory and CPU work are spr: Controls how memory and CPU work are spread on systems with more than one memory node or CPU socket. Most desktop PCs should leave this off.
strings.Maps to llama.cpp --numa distribute, iso: Maps to llama.cpp --numa distribute, isolate, or numactl. These modes change thread and memory locality on NUMA hardware; a wrong policy can increase cross-node traffic and reduce performance.
strings.Extends supported models beyond their or: Extends supported models beyond their original context length. It can handle longer input, but may reduce quality if the model or profile was not designed for it.
strings.Forces YaRN/RoPE scaling instead of foll: Forces YaRN/RoPE scaling instead of following the matched YAML profile. AutoTuner derives the required factor from requested versus native context and emits the corresponding rope-scaling arguments. Turning it off keeps the native positional scale.
strings.Sets how far the model's positional rang: Sets how far the model's positional range is stretched. 1.0 means no extension; higher values target proportionally longer context.
strings.Used as the YaRN/RoPE scale factor when: Used as the YaRN/RoPE scale factor when scaling is active. A factor that is too low cannot cover the requested context; an unnecessarily high factor can harm short-context accuracy. Manual mode accepts the value exactly as entered.
strings.Controls randomness. Lower values are mo: Controls randomness. Lower values are more predictable; higher values are more varied but can become less reliable.
strings.Passed as --temp and rescales token logi: Passed as --temp and rescales token logits before sampling. 0 is effectively deterministic in common llama.cpp sampling paths; the best nonzero value depends on the model and the other samplers.
strings.Limits each next-token choice to the K m: Limits each next-token choice to the K most likely candidates. Smaller values are more focused; 0 disables this filter.
strings.Passed as --top-k. The sampler removes e: Passed as --top-k. The sampler removes every token outside the top K before later probability filters run. Very small K can make output repetitive; large K approaches an unrestricted candidate set.
strings.Keeps the smallest group of likely token: Keeps the smallest group of likely tokens whose combined chance reaches this value. Lower values are safer and narrower.
Passed as --top-p for nucleus sampling. At 1.0 it removes almost nothing; lower thresholds dynamically trim the probability tail. It interacts with temperature, top-k, and min-p in sampler order.
strings.Drops tokens that are far less likely th: Drops tokens that are far less likely than the current best choice. Higher values make output more focused.
strings.Passed as --min-p. A candidate must meet: Passed as --min-p. A candidate must meet a probability floor relative to the highest-probability token, making the filter adapt to model confidence. 0 disables it; excessive values can reduce diversity.
strings.Discourages the model from repeating rec: Discourages the model from repeating recent words or patterns. 1.0 means no penalty; slightly higher values reduce loops.
strings.Passed as --repeat-penalty and modifies: Passed as --repeat-penalty and modifies logits for tokens found in the repeat window. Values that are too high can damage code, names, formatting, and intentional repetition.
strings.Encourages introducing new tokens instea: Encourages introducing new tokens instead of reusing ones already present. Positive values increase novelty; 0 leaves it neutral.
strings.Passed as --presence-penalty. Unlike a c: Passed as --presence-penalty. Unlike a count-based frequency penalty, it applies based on whether a token appeared at all. Negative values encourage reuse; strong positive values can hurt coherent code or terminology.
strings.Limits how many tokens the faster draft: Limits how many tokens the faster draft path may propose per step. 0 uses the tested model profile; larger values are not automatically faster.
strings.Passed as --spec-draft-n-max N when an e: Passed as --spec-draft-n-max N when an external -md drafter or embedded MTP head is active. 0 uses draft_max from the matched YAML profile (fallback 2). The main model must verify every proposal, and on AMD/Vulkan values above roughly 2–3 often add overhead.
strings.Chooses how much internal reasoning a co: Chooses how much internal reasoning a compatible model should use. Auto leaves the decision to the model; Off requests no reasoning.
strings.Minimal through extra_high are sent as r: Minimal through extra_high are sent as reasoning_effort via --chat-template-kwargs. Off emits --reasoning off; Auto emits no override. Support and accepted names depend on the model's Jinja template and llama.cpp build.
strings.Caps how many tokens a reasoning model m: Caps how many tokens a reasoning model may spend thinking before it must answer. -1 leaves it unlimited; 0 asks it to skip thinking.
strings.Positive values emit --reasoning-budget: Positive values emit --reasoning-budget N on compatible llama.cpp builds. -1 emits no budget flag. This budget consumes context/output tokens and is separate from the qualitative reasoning-effort hint.
strings.Keeps earlier assistant thinking traces: Keeps earlier assistant thinking traces available in later turns when the model supports that behaviour.
strings.Passed as --reasoning-preserve. Compatib: Passed as --reasoning-preserve. Compatible chat templates retain reasoning content in conversation history instead of stripping it. This can improve continuity but increases prompt/context usage and may expose prior reasoning to clients. Since llama.cpp b10786 the server enables preserved reasoning by default whenever the template supports it; unticked leaves that default alone. Add --no-reasoning-preserve to Extra CLI flags to force it off.
strings.Adds advanced llama-server options that: Adds advanced llama-server options that AutoTuner does not expose elsewhere. Use this only when you know the exact flag syntax.
strings.The text is parsed into arguments and ap: The text is parsed into arguments and appended to the generated command after modeled settings. Unsupported, duplicated, or unsafe flags can override assumptions or make startup fail; normal shell expansion is not used.
strings.Adds, removes, or temporarily disables f: Adds, removes, or temporarily disables folders containing llama.cpp builds.
strings.AutoTuner scans enabled roots for runnab: AutoTuner scans enabled roots for runnable llama-server binaries and compatible sibling fork directories. Paths are stored per operating system so one settings file can be shared across dual-boot installs.
strings.Chooses the balance between speed, conte: Chooses the balance between speed, context capacity, and memory headroom. Balanced is the best starting point for most users.
strings.Selects conversational or code-focused g: Selects conversational or code-focused generation behaviour. Chat is more varied; Coding is usually more deterministic.
strings.The matched model profile supplies mode-: The matched model profile supplies mode-specific temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, repetition, and presence settings. Profiles without a coding block fall back to chat values; model placement and memory planning are unchanged.
strings.Auto chooses a GPU from current free mem: Auto chooses a GPU from current free memory. Selecting a card forces the next server onto only that GPU, which is useful for running a second model on another card.
strings.A card selection persists as forced_gpu: A card selection persists as forced_gpu and mirrors CLI --gpu. The launch environment hides the other devices and sets the matching backend/main-GPU index. Auto keeps all eligible cards visible and uses live VRAM-aware placement.
strings.Shows or hides language, font, update, a: Shows or hides language, font, update, and application settings.
strings.The secondary toolbar is click-persisten: The secondary toolbar is click-persistent: it remains open while the pointer moves elsewhere and closes only when this ellipsis is clicked again.
strings.Built-in JSON packs fall back to English: Built-in JSON packs fall back to English (UK) for unknown strings. Custom packs are validated and copied into ~/.autotuner/languages.
strings.Opens the folder for your own JSON langu: Opens the folder for your own JSON language packs.
strings.AutoTuner creates an English-based custo: AutoTuner creates an English-based custom-language-template.json there once. Edit its ID, name, locale, and translations, then choose Custom language pack… to validate and activate it.
strings.Checks GitHub for a newer AutoTuner vers: Checks GitHub for a newer AutoTuner version and installs it while keeping your personal settings.
strings.Source checkouts update through git or a: Source checkouts update through git or a source ZIP. Frozen builds download the OS-specific GitHub Release ZIP and use a restart swap helper. autotuner_settings.json is backed up and restored around either update path.
strings.Opens application-wide startup and windo: Opens application-wide startup and window behaviour options.
strings.These opt-in preferences are shared by s: These opt-in preferences are shared by source and frozen builds through ~/.autotuner. They do not change model tuning, generated llama-server arguments, or per-model Expert overrides.
strings.Filters the model list while you type so: Filters the model list while you type so large collections are easier to navigate.
strings.The case-insensitive text filter changes: The case-insensitive text filter changes only which already-scanned model entries are visible. It does not rescan folders, modify files, or change the currently selected model's saved settings.
strings.Shows every model in the familiar flat l: Shows every model in the familiar flat list.
strings.Favorites stay sorted first. Switching v: Favorites stay sorted first. Switching views keeps the active filter and selected model and does not rescan or move any files.
strings.Groups models by their real folder and s: Groups models by their real folder and subfolder hierarchy.
strings.Click folder rows to expand or collapse: Click folder rows to expand or collapse them. Favorites are also shown in a separate section at the top while remaining visible in their original folders.
strings.Switches instantly between untouched Aut: Switches instantly between untouched Auto tuning, the measured performance winner, and four personal setting profiles.
strings.Profiles are isolated by model, performa: Profiles are isolated by model, performance mode, selected draft head, and execution backend. Perform Vulkan, Perform HIP, Perform CPU, and other detected backends stay independent and disabled until measured. Editing Auto or Perform in Expert settings forks the change into a Custom slot instead of overwriting either source.
strings.Opens detailed controls for context, mem: Opens detailed controls for context, memory placement, sampling, reasoning, parallel requests, and server flags.
strings.Expert values are stored per model. Auto: Expert values are stored per model. Auto mode re-fits dependent values around your overrides; Manual mode constructs the launch configuration directly and can create unsupported or unsafe combinations.
strings.Explains what AutoTuner detected about t: Explains what AutoTuner detected about the selected model and why it chose the shown configuration.
strings.The report includes GGUF metadata inputs: The report includes GGUF metadata inputs, architecture and MoE/hybrid classification, KV-size math, context and memory capacity estimates, matched profile data, and warnings useful for technical debugging.
strings.Measures realistic prompt and generation: Measures realistic prompt and generation speed and saves an independent optimized profile for every selected performance mode.
strings.Runs fresh private loopback llama-server: Runs fresh private loopback llama-server instances with either the standard 12.5% prompt (65,536-token cap) or a custom 0.01–100% uncapped prompt, plus 256 n_decode tokens. It can test all four performance targets, all benchmarkable models, optional YaRN, and optional MTP/draft depths. CPU threads and batch settings are swept and confirmed; the fastest mode is reported, remembered per model, and selected. Exact contexts above the static safe estimate are saved only after the real server proves them. No hardware overclock setting is changed.
strings.Shows summaries in-app and opens a detai: Shows summaries in-app and opens a detailed browser report for every run.
strings.Quick pass, Standard 12.5%, and Custom e: Quick pass, Standard 12.5%, and Custom evidence is grouped separately; legacy 25% records migrate to Custom. The self-contained HTML expands every candidate's settings, samples, PP/decode/end-to-end charts, drafter variant, and drafted-token acceptance without external assets.
strings.Keeps the vision projector in system mem: Keeps the vision projector in system memory. This frees GPU memory for the model or context, but image processing becomes slower.
strings.Emits --no-mmproj-offload. The projector: Emits --no-mmproj-offload. The projector's estimated footprint moves from VRAM to RAM in AutoTuner's budget; text-token generation is mostly unaffected after image encoding, while each image prefill uses CPU execution.
strings.Speeds up repetitive text or code by reu: Speeds up repetitive text or code by reusing patterns already found in the current context. It needs no separate draft model.
strings.Enables ngram-mod self-speculative decod: Enables ngram-mod self-speculative decoding, which builds a rolling hash lookup table of roughly 16 MiB and proposes matching token sequences. Gains are workload-dependent and strongest for code edits, summaries, or repeated reasoning patterns.
strings.Keeps reusable prompt beginnings in syst: Keeps reusable prompt beginnings in system RAM so repeated long instructions can reach the first generated token faster.
strings.Enables llama-server --cache-ram. Matchi: Enables llama-server --cache-ram. Matching system prompts, RAG scaffolds, or coding-agent preambles can skip part of prompt evaluation. The configured MiB limit is included in RAM planning; multimodal prompt reuse requires llama.cpp b10045 or newer.
strings.Limits how much system memory prompt cac: Limits how much system memory prompt caching may use. 2048 MiB is a bounded default; 0 disables the cache and -1 allows it to grow.
strings.Passed as --cache-ram / -cram. Positive: Passed as --cache-ram / -cram. Positive values cap the host cache in MiB and are added to AutoTuner's RAM estimate. Unlimited mode keeps a safety reserve but can still grow until llama-server eviction or system memory pressure intervenes.
strings.Allows supported reasoning models to use: Allows supported reasoning models to use their thinking mode. Turn it off for shorter, direct answers when the template supports that.
strings.This per-model launch option controls wh: This per-model launch option controls whether AutoTuner applies the model/profile reasoning path. Exact flags and output separation depend on the selected chat template and llama.cpp build; Expert settings can further choose effort, token budget, and history preservation.
strings.Sets which network address the model ser: Sets which network address the model server listens on. Keep 127.0.0.1 if only programs on this computer should connect.
strings.Passed as llama-server --host. 127.0.0.1: Passed as llama-server --host. 127.0.0.1 is loopback-only; 0.0.0.0 or a LAN address can expose the OpenAI-compatible API, metrics, and slots endpoints to other devices. AutoTuner does not add authentication or a firewall rule.
strings.Sets the starting network port for model: Sets the starting network port for model servers. The first server normally uses 1234 and additional servers receive the next free port.
strings.The validated value is persisted as base: The validated value is persisted as base_port and passed as --port after adding the manual offset and checking active server collisions. Stopped servers release their port for reuse; valid ports are in the 1–65535 range.
strings.Adds 0–10 to the base port, making it ea: Adds 0–10 to the base port, making it easy to keep separate AutoTuner instances or environments on predictable ports.
strings.The persisted offset is added before Aut: The persisted offset is added before AutoTuner searches for collisions with its managed servers. For example, base 1234 plus offset 2 starts at 1236, then later concurrent servers use subsequent free ports.
strings.Selects which running model server the s: Selects which running model server the status and Stop controls refer to.
strings.Entries track a managed process, model,: Entries track a managed process, model, port, readiness, slot state, GPU placement, and estimated VRAM footprint. Changing the selection does not stop or restart any server.
strings.Shows or completely hides AutoTuner's bo: Shows or completely hides AutoTuner's bottom status panel.
strings.Moves the vertical splitter to restore i: Moves the vertical splitter to restore its previous size or collapse the panel to zero. It affects only the interface layout; the separate llama-server terminal and log generation continue unchanged.
strings.Opens the document workflow for the sele: Opens the document workflow for the selected OCR model.
strings.Accepts images, PDF, Word, OpenDocument,: Accepts images, PDF, Word, OpenDocument, presentation, and spreadsheet inputs. Office files are converted with LibreOffice, PDF pages are rendered with PyMuPDF, and normalized images are sent to the same llama-server chat-completions API used by the terminal workflow.
strings.Starts the selected model with the shown: Starts the selected model with the shown Auto or Expert configuration. Existing servers can keep running.
strings.AutoTuner resolves a compatible binary,: AutoTuner resolves a compatible binary, validates memory and flags, builds the llama-server command, selects the requested or emptier GPU, assigns the next free port, and tracks the new process and health endpoint.
strings.Stops only the server currently selected: Stops only the server currently selected in the Server list.
strings.Requests a graceful termination of the t: Requests a graceful termination of the tracked terminal process, then uses the platform-specific fallback if needed. Other managed servers remain active and the released port becomes reusable.
strings.Stops every model server that this AutoT: Stops every model server that this AutoTuner window launched.
strings.Iterates over the managed server registr: Iterates over the managed server registry and performs the same graceful, platform-aware process shutdown for each entry. Unrelated llama-server processes started elsewhere are not targeted.
strings.Closes AutoTuner completely instead of h: Closes AutoTuner completely instead of hiding it in the notification area.
strings.Sets the explicit-quit path, asks for co: Sets the explicit-quit path, asks for confirmation when managed servers are active, shuts them down, saves window state, removes the tray icon, and exits the application process.
strings.The window disappears when you click X,: The window disappears when you click X, but AutoTuner and its servers keep running in the notification area.
strings.The close event is redirected to QSystem: The close event is redirected to QSystemTrayIcon.hide() instead of ending the process. Restore the window from the tray icon; use its Quit action or AutoTuner's Quit button for a full, graceful shutdown of managed servers.
strings.This option cannot be used because no no: This option cannot be used because no notification area was detected on this desktop.
strings.Qt reports that QSystemTrayIcon is unava: Qt reports that QSystemTrayIcon is unavailable, so hiding the window would leave no reliable way to restore it. AutoTuner therefore disables the setting and keeps normal X-to-close behaviour.
strings.Choose one or more folders that contain: Choose one or more folders that contain your GGUF models.

strings.Scans the configured model folders again: Scans the configured model folders again and refreshes the list.
strings.Runs GGUF discovery and metadata matchin: Runs GGUF discovery and metadata matching in a background worker, then rebuilds model, mmproj, draft/MTP, and profile associations without freezing the interface.
strings.Makes all interface text smaller or larg: Makes all interface text smaller or larger.
strings.Changes the QApplication font size by on: Changes the QApplication font size by one point within the 7–22 point range, reapplies it to the monospace preview/log widgets, and persists the result for the next launch.

Hover for how this metric is collected.

strings.Prompt processing (PP): llama.cpp's nati: Prompt processing (PP): llama.cpp's native prompt_per_second timing after an excluded warm-up (or prompt_n / prompt_ms when the direct field is unavailable). The deterministic prompt uses each run's saved context fraction. Only Standard is capped at 65,536 prompt tokens; Custom is uncapped. Prompt caching is disabled.
strings.n_decode: llama.cpp's native predicted_p: n_decode: llama.cpp's native predicted_per_second timing (or predicted_n / predicted_ms fallback). AutoTuner requests 256 deterministic decode tokens with EOS ignored and uses the median of the accepted samples.
strings.End-to-end: (prompt tokens + generated t: End-to-end: (prompt tokens + generated tokens) divided by native prompt time plus native decode time for this exact workload. This is the score used to rank candidates and performance modes.
strings.Selects which llama.cpp build starts the: Selects which llama.cpp build starts the server. AutoTuner can choose a more compatible build for a specific model when needed.
strings.The selected directory supplies llama-se: The selected directory supplies llama-server or the matching diffusion binary. Model YAML profiles may override this default for required forks or features. Build discovery scans the enabled llama.cpp roots configured with the adjacent llama Builds button.
strings.Conservative. KV reserved for 128k (MoE): Conservative. KV reserved for 128k (MoE) / 64k (dense) context, generous safety bands. Single slot with the full context. Pick this for long-context sessions.
strings.Default. KV reserved for 64k (MoE) / 32k: Default. KV reserved for 64k (MoE) / 32k (dense) context — enough headroom for most chats while letting more weight/expert layers fit on GPU. Single slot.
strings.Aggressive. KV reserved for only 32k (Mo: Aggressive. KV reserved for only 32k (MoE) / 16k (dense) — every spare GB of VRAM goes to weight/expert layers for max tokens/s. Single slot. Not recommended for very long context.
strings.Max context for low-VRAM / high-RAM syst: Max context for low-VRAM / high-RAM systems (e.g. 8 GB VRAM, 64 GB RAM). KV cache moves to system RAM (--no-kv-offload), trading generation speed for far larger context — the only way to reach 90k+ on a 20 GB MoE that barely fits the GPU. Single parallel slot.
strings.When AutoTuner starts because you signed: When AutoTuner starts because you signed in, it opens without a window: in the notification area if Hide on close is on, otherwise minimized on the taskbar.
strings.Applies only to the login entry, which p: Applies only to the login entry, which passes --autostart; manual starts always show the window. Until you save a choice here it follows Hide on close. Servers, the control API and background scans start as usual; restore the window from the tray icon, the taskbar, or by launching AutoTuner again.

profile_notes.deepseek-v4_1.yaml: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: a multimodal 552B-backbone Causal Encoder-Decoder MoE (deepseek41 architecture: CSA2 attention that shares KV across layers, Engram conditional memory, single-pass mHC) with up to 1,048,576 tokens of context. Mainline llama.cpp runs it since b11870 (PR #31086), including image input through the deepseek41v mmproj and its own chat formatting. There is no in-file MTP head; DSpark speculation uses a separate DFLASH draft GGUF (draft-dspark). AutoTuner budgets KV for every layer, which overestimates the shared CSA2 cache; the plan has not been measured on a real V4.1 GGUF. GGUFs from the earlier conversion-only PR #28696 are refused. Sampling from the model card: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95; reasoning effort runs from 1 to 100.
profile_notes.nex-n2_5-mini.yaml: Nex-AGI Nex-N2.5-mini is a 35B multimodal Qwen3.5-MoE derivative (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration; GGUF qwen35moe), with 40 layers, attention every fourth layer, 256 experts/top-8 and 262,144 native context. Both chat and coding use the publisher's temperature 0.7 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 40. Keep the Nex chat template embedded in the GGUF, not a generic Qwen replacement. On llama.cpp pass reasoning_effort via chat_template_kwargs: none disables thinking, medium is adaptive (default), high always thinks. enable_thinking is not this template's switch. --jinja handles its Qwen3-Coder-style tools; SGLang's --tool-call-parser and --reasoning-parser flags must not be copied to llama.cpp. Vision needs the matching mmproj. MTP is available only when the converted GGUF retains the declared NextN layer; no YaRN extension is enabled by default. Source: https://huggingface.co/nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-mini.
profile_notes.glm-5_3-cybersecurity.yaml: Profile for dealignai/GLM-5.3-CYBERSECURITY-FP8 and its GGUF conversions, not an official Z.ai Cyber SKU or GLM-5.3-Flash. Its config.json matches Z.ai GLM-5.3: glm-dsa architecture, 1,048,576 native context, same KV/MTP contract. A separate profile preserves the publisher's repetition_penalty 1.1 instead of base GLM's 1.0. Temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95 are unchanged; top_k 40 / min_p 0.01 retain AutoTuner's local GLM defaults. The derivative's embedded template defaults clear_thinking to true, unlike upstream false; --no-reasoning-preserve honors that default rather than forcing base reasoning retention. Keep the derivative's embedded template. The model-card 131,072 limit is a vLLM deployment example, not the native context ceiling. FP8 Safetensors cannot be loaded directly by llama.cpp: select a compatible GGUF. No vLLM flags are added to llama.cpp. Source: https://huggingface.co/dealignai/GLM-5.3-CYBERSECURITY-FP8.
profile_notes.minicpm5-2b.yaml: MiniCPM5-2B (also labelled 2.6B in the official GGUF) is a dense text-only llama model with 42 layers and native 131,072-token context. It works with mainline llama.cpp. OpenBMB recommends temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95 for Think mode; do not inherit the 1B profile's 0.7/0.9 temperatures. Thinking remains controlled by the embedded template (enable_thinking). No vision, MTP or unverified RoPE extension is assumed. Sources: https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B and https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM/blob/main/docs/deployment/llama_cpp.md.
profile_notes.k2-horizon.yaml: IFM K2 Horizon is NOT Moonshot Kimi-K2. Mainline llama.cpp b11454+ (PR #29535) loads the dense models and MoVA-36B-A4B with a dedicated chat parser; the MBZUAI-IFM model/K2Horizon fork works as well. MoVA-36B-A4B has 48 full-attention layers, 100 FFN experts (8 active), 64 value experts (4 active), three leading dense layers and native 524,288-token context. MoVA combines values before caching: KV is not multiplied by the value-expert count. --n-cpu-moe does not move the value experts, so Auto uses whole-layer offload instead of the FFN-only expert estimate. Use the GGUF's embedded template; high reasoning and XML tools are the author's defaults. No vision, MTP or RoPE extension. Sources: https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B-GGUF and llama.cpp PR #29535.
profile_notes.kolibri-1.yaml: Aleph Alpha Kolibri 1: a 78B-total/3.5B-active MoE reasoning model for German and English (kolibri1 architecture, 384 experts with 6 active plus a shared expert, sliding-window attention, 262,144 tokens of context). Mainline llama.cpp loads it since b11709 (PR #30673); the hob-llama.cpp release hob-b11434 still works as well. GGUFs made with the earlier hob patch store the pre-tokenizer "kolibri1" and gating type 5, which mainline does not know; on mainline AutoTuner maps them to the equivalent qwen2 pre-tokenizer and sigmoid gating with --override-kv. Measured on b12187 (Q4_K_M, both GPUs plus CPU experts): 67 tok/s on Vulkan, 63 on HIP. Reasoning effort none/low/medium/high is set through the chat template; sampling from the GGUF: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.97, top-k 128.
profile_notes.spark2_5.yaml: Spark-X2.5-1.7B and Spark-X2.5-4B use the spark2_5 architecture added in llama.cpp b10828 (PR #27868), fused QKV and head-wise sigmoid attention gates. Use the embedded Spark2.5 template for reasoning/tool calls, not a Qwen template. Native context is 1,048,576 tokens; available RAM/VRAM determines the actual safe window. Q8 KV is preferred; no speculative MTP head is assumed. Layer/head counts and the 3:1 sliding/full-attention pattern come from GGUF, not a fixed 1.7B assumption. Both sizes share the official sampling defaults. Sources: https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B and https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27868.
profile_notes.hy4-mainline.yaml: Mainline support for Tencent HY4 Preview with general.architecture=hy_v4 landed in PR #28127 (first available local release tag b10813). The older AngelSlim hyv4 GGUF format remains a separate patched-runtime profile; renaming its metadata does not convert its tensors. Official HY4 sampling and native 1M context are shared, but memory remains hardware-limited. The stock converter drops nextn/MTP layers; its GGUF does not contain an embedded drafter on b10839. Source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28127.
profile_notes._default.yaml: Fallback profile. It is used whenever no specific profile matches. Chat defaults are deliberately conservative (temp 0.7); coding is clearly more deterministic (temp 0.2). Model-specific YAML files override this.
profile_notes.agents-a1.yaml: Agents-A1 (InternScience, 2026, Apache 2.0) is a 35B-A3B MoE agent model post-trained on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (GGUF architecture "qwen35moe", hybrid GatedDeltaNet + full attention; the scanner counts the KV cache correctly through recurrent_layers). This profile matches only by the filename pattern ("agents-a1"); re-quants without that name correctly fall back to the qwen3_5-3_6 architecture fallback. Native 256k context (YaRN up to ~1M). Sampling uses the official card values temp=0.85 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=20 / rep=1.0; presence_penalty is set to 0.0 instead of the official 1.1 because presence_penalty reproducibly causes loops during tool calling (see qwen3_5-3_6.yaml); for pure chat use: -- --presence-penalty 1.1. Reasoning model (<think> blocks, Qwen3 parser) with native function calling. Tip: `--jinja` at start cleanly separates <think> into the reasoning_content field and parses <tool_call> blocks as OpenAI-style tool_calls: -- --jinja. CAUTION when downloading: InternScience/Agents-A1 itself is Safetensors; use the GGUF repositories for the tuner (for example InternScience/Agents-A1-Q4_K_M-GGUF or LordNeel/Agents-A1-GGUF). A current llama.cpp mainline with qwen35moe support is required (b9963 is fine).
profile_notes.bailingmoe2-5.yaml: InclusionAI (Ant Group) Ling-2.6-flash is a MoE with hybrid attention, architecture "bailingmoe2.5" / "bailing_hybrid". CAUTION (as of b9739): NOT in vanilla llama.cpp; it needs a Ling-2.6-capable fork (for example ik_llama.cpp). Select that fork in the GUI's fork dropdown; the GGUF already declares the architecture and will run on mainline without re-downloading once BailingMoeV2.5 is merged there. Normal autoregressive server model. Sampling follows the InclusionAI recommendation temp=0.7 / top_p=0.8 / rep=1.05; coding is more deterministic. --jinja for template/reasoning. Ling/Ring 2.0 ("bailingmoe2", mainline) is handled by ling-ring.yaml.
profile_notes.bonsai-2-27b.yaml: PrismML Ternary-Bonsai 2 27B on a Qwen3.8-27B hybrid-attention base: end-to-end ternary weights (1.72 bits per weight), thinking by default, tool calling, optional vision projector (mmproj Q8_0 0.63 GB or BF16 0.93 GB), 262k native context. Two packings of the same weights: PTQ1_0 (dense trits, 1.75 bpw, 5.95 GB) and PQ2_0 (2-bit slots, 2.13 bpw, 7.21 GB). Both are Prism-private ggml types (143 / 142) with a Hadamard activation transform: they need the PrismML prism fork built by the Ternary/Bonsai recipes (2b_ builds, prism-b10687 or newer); mainline llama.cpp rejects them as unknown tensor types. The recipes pin prism-b10743, whose Vulkan backend runs both packings on the GPU (prism-b10687 had no Vulkan PQ2_0 path); HIP/CUDA run both. Mainline llama.cpp b11556+ (PR #29600) loads the Hadamard fold too, but only for mainline conversions (Q2_0, F16); for PTQ1_0/PQ2_0 AutoTuner still requires the fork. Official thinking-mode sampling (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20).
profile_notes.bonsai-2.yaml: PrismML Ternary-Bonsai 2 2B, 4B and 9B on Qwen3.8 backbones with Hadamard-folded ternary weights and 262,144 tokens of context. The Q2_0 GGUFs run on mainline llama.cpp b11556+ (PR #29600) and on the PrismML prism fork; an older mainline build lacks the prism.hadamard loader and would decode garbage, so AutoTuner refuses it. PQ2_0/PTQ1_0 packings and the separate MTP/DFlash2 files still need the prism fork. Thinking-mode sampling as for Bonsai 2 27B: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20.
profile_notes.bonsai-27b.yaml: PrismML Bonsai 27B on a Qwen3.6-27B base: multimodal, thinking- and tool-calling-capable, 262k native context. The Q1_0-g128 language weights take about 3.9 GB; the optional vision projector takes another roughly 0.63 GB. Current mainline llama.cpp supports Q1_0 on CPU, Metal, CUDA, and Vulkan. PrismML's Q4_0 KV cache saves considerable memory at very long context but is not a speed feature.
profile_notes.bonsai-ternary-27b.yaml: PrismML Ternary-Bonsai 27B on a Qwen3.6-27B base: multimodal, thinking- and tool-calling-capable, 262k native context. The Q2_0-g128 weights ({-1, 0, +1}) take about 7.2 GB; the optional vision projector another roughly 0.63 GB. Use the PrismML prism fork for the published Q2_0-g128 file. The separate Q2_0_g64 file is intended for current mainline llama.cpp (currently CPU/Metal; further backends follow).
profile_notes.bonsai-ternary.yaml: Ternary-Bonsai (8B/4B/1.7B): weights in {-1, 0, +1} (1.58 bits per weight). Between 1-bit Bonsai and full precision: about 9x smaller, 5x faster, and better on benchmarks than 1-bit Bonsai (avg +5 points). Q2_0 is the storage format used (2-bit aligned for Metal/CUDA). Requires the PrismML 2b_llama.cpp fork (ternary kernels, 2-bit Q2_0).
profile_notes.bonsai.yaml: PrismML Bonsai 8B is the first commercially viable 1-bit LLM (Q1_0 GGUF, ~1.15 GB). Competitive with full-precision 8B models while 14x smaller and 8x faster on edge hardware. Requires the PrismML fork of llama.cpp (1b_llama.cpp), not mainline. The Q1_0 quant is merged upstream for CPU/Metal/CUDA/Vulkan, but AMD ROCm and the optimised x86 paths still need the fork. The coding profile is only slightly lowered (0.3) instead of an aggressive 0.15: at extremely low temperatures 1-bit quants tend to loop.
profile_notes.clef.yaml: Cloudflare Clef / Clef-Flash: a joint decision model on a Qwen3.5 backbone (architecture clef, llama.cpp b11371+). A server running Clef serves only POST /v1/systemone; text generation is unavailable, so chat, sampling, reasoning and speculation settings have no effect. All questions of a request are read in one prompt and decided jointly; that prompt must fit into one physical batch, which AutoTuner sizes for 8192 tokens. Up to 255 options per choice question. Images need b11418+, the Clef mmproj and a GGUF converted on 2026-10-05 or later; AutoTuner warns about older conversions, whose template has no image slot.
profile_notes.cohere2moe.yaml: Cohere North-Mini-Code-1.0: 30B total / 3B active MoE for agentic coding (tool use, repository tasks, browser automation), Apache-2.0, architecture "cohere2moe" (cohere2 iSWA attention + glm4moe-style sigmoid gating, 1 leading dense + 48 MoE layers, 128 experts / 8 active). NOTE: cohere2moe has been in llama.cpp mainline since b9626 (PR #24260), so on b9829 it runs without a fork or PR branch; only builds before b9626 still need the PR branch. Normal autoregressive server model (no diffusion path). Sampling follows the Cohere/Unsloth recommendation (temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95) in chat; the coding profile is more deterministic (0.6) for stable tool calls. --jinja is mandatory (chat template + tool parsing).
profile_notes.cohere_command_r.yaml: Specialised in RAG and tool calling. Low temperature already in chat mode because Command R/R+ is meant to cite from sources: "chat" here is document-grounded conversation rather than free writing. The coding profile is almost greedy (0.1) for deterministic tool calls and structured output.
profile_notes.decision-systemone.yaml: TypeSafe-style decision models (OpenJev, lev, Laya, Julia-1, Kev, Nimble, Perplexity pplx-decider, LiquidAI d1-3B, d1-2B, d1-omni-600M and d1-omni-2B, vLLM Decision 2 and D3, H2O-Lightning-4B, MiniCPM-OCR-Jev): they answer typed choice/score/noul questions about a state in one forward pass through POST /v1/systemone and generate no text, so chat, sampling, reasoning and speculation settings have no effect. Needs llama.cpp b11364+ (b11361 for all but Nimble); AutoTuner reads the GGUF's decision type and requires b11447+ for pplx-decider, b11483+ for d1-3B, b11488+ for d1-omni-600M, b11571+ for vllm-decision2, b11577+ for vllm-d3, b11773+ for H2O-Lightning-4B, b11928+ for MiniCPM-OCR-Jev and b11945+ for LiquidAI d1-2B and d1-omni-2B (Granite Switch 4.1, a chat model with a decision adapter, needs b11707+). The vllm-sr Decision-2.0 GGUFs use the fork-only type decision2, which mainline rejects; AutoTuner names the fork they need. The encoder variants (Laya, Julia-1, d1-omni-600M, vLLM Decision 2 and D3) must fit the whole prompt into one physical batch, which AutoTuner sizes for up to 8192 tokens. OpenJev, pplx-decider and the d1 models accept images when their mmproj is attached (d1-omni-600M also audio). Probabilities use the temperatures stored in the GGUF and are not guaranteed to be calibrated for your data. The prompt cache stays off, as in llama.cpp b11642+: decision states seldom repeat.
profile_notes.deepseek-ocr.yaml: DeepSeek-OCR v1/v2 document model. The verified prompt is "Free OCR."; Unlimited-OCR is a distinct checkpoint with the same GGUF architecture and uses its own name-matched profile and "document parsing." prompt.
profile_notes.deepseek-r1-v3.yaml: DeepSeek-V3.2 (671B MoE / 37B active) with DSA for efficient long-context attention, or R1 (reasoning). The R1 and V3.2 models use <think> tags for chain-of-thought. The coding profile uses temp=0.3 (vs. 1.0 chat) for more deterministic final code while the reasoning chain stays "creative". CAUTION: the Speciale variant (V3.2-Speciale) does NOT support tool calling.
profile_notes.deepseek-v4.yaml: DeepSeek-V4 Pro (1.6T-A49B) and Flash (284B-A13B) are 1M-context MoE models with the dedicated deepseek4 GGUF architecture. Base architecture support started earlier, but this combined Pro/Flash profile requires llama.cpp b10254+ for the dedicated V4-Flash chat-template contract; a current build is strongly preferred for later backend/indexer and KV fixes. Official decoding defaults are temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0. Think-Max workflows should reserve at least a 384k context window. These are datacenter-scale models; local workstation use needs very aggressive quantization plus large system RAM and CPU expert offload. Keep preserved reasoning for long agent/tool sessions. llama.cpp b10786 adds the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp projector (deepseek4v mmproj) and the image-token routing bias; vision needs that build plus a matching mmproj file, and image spans attend bidirectionally inside the sliding window.
profile_notes.devstral.yaml: Optimised for code completion (Cline, Aider, VS Code). The coding profile (temp=0.15) gives deterministic completion; the chat profile (temp=0.4) suits code explanations and discussion.
profile_notes.diffusion-gemma.yaml: DiffusionGemma is a diffusion text model (not an autoregressive GGUF for the normal llama-server). It runs through llama-diffusion-gemma-server (PR #24427), a SEPARATE OpenAI-compatible HTTP server with /health, /v1/chat/completions, /props, and port binding. Select your diffusion build in the GUI's fork dropdown (for example "d_bXXXX_vulkan_llama.cpp" or "d_bXXXX_hip_llama.cpp"); AutoTuner finds llama-diffusion-gemma-server inside it automatically, no path needs to be hard-coded. The server stays queryable (chat UI, RooCode, OpenAI clients); port and state behave like any other server. Mainline b9700 does not recognise the "diffusion-gemma" architecture; AutoTuner still detects it (is_diffusion) and automatically selects the gemma-server runner. Mainline diffusion models (Dream/LLaDA/RND1) have NO server of their own and instead run single-shot through llama-diffusion-cli. Scheduling: EITHER --diffusion-eps OR --diffusion-block-length, not both (DiffusionGemma uses block scheduling). Fork-specific flags must be enabled through diffusion.fork_args if your build knows them. IMPORTANT for VRAM: DiffusionGemma has an extremely large F16 KV cache (k/v_length=512, 5x normal). Auto is therefore capped at 4096 (KV ~0.47 GiB); 8192 can, with allocator overhead, reach a contiguous 1 GiB Vulkan allocation and crash despite free total VRAM. The calculation also reserves 1.5 GiB of diffusion runtime overhead. Pinning to the 32 GB R9700 happens automatically (env_overrides).
profile_notes.dots1.yaml: rednote-hilab dots.llm1: MoE, 142B total / 14B active (Instruct + Base), architecture "dots1", native 32k context, performance at Qwen2.5-72B level. rednote's card gives no explicit sampler recommendation, so conservative middle-of-the-road defaults are used (temp 0.7 chat / 0.3 coding); adjust to the generation_config if needed. With only 14B active parameters plus --n-cpu-moe it runs well on a 32 GB card.
profile_notes.embeddinggemma-2.yaml: Google EmbeddingGemma 2 (architecture gemma-embedding2, llama.cpp b11452+): a multimodal embedding model with a 270M non-causal text encoder, mean pooling and 768-dimensional output (Matryoshka truncation to 512/256/128; re-normalize after truncating). NO chat/completion: the profile starts an embedding endpoint (--embeddings, pooling from the GGUF). Context is 8,192 tokens, read in one physical batch. Prefix queries with the model card's task instruction, e.g. "task: search result | query: ...", and documents with "title: none | text: ...". The vision/audio projector (mmproj) is a separate file; text embeddings are what AutoTuner validates.
profile_notes.ernie-4_5.yaml: Baidu ERNIE 4.5: MoE family, Apache-2.0, architecture "ernie4_5-moe". Variants: 300B-A47B (datacenter/cluster) and 21B-A3B (local, also as a Thinking edition), native context up to 131072. Sampling is conservative (temp 0.8 / top_p 0.8 chat, 0.6 coding) because Baidu publishes no prominent unified llama.cpp recommendation; adjust to the generation_config of the specific variant if needed. --jinja for the chat template / thinking separation. 21B-A3B (3B active) runs well with --n-cpu-moe on a 32 GB card.
profile_notes.exaone-4_5.yaml: LG AI Research EXAONE 4.5: LG's first open-weight VLM, 33B total (31.7B core + 1.29B vision), DENSE, text+image, 256k context. Hybrid attention (3x SWA-4096 + 1x global NoPE, 16x), 64 layers. IMPORTANT licence: non-commercial, research/academic only, no production use (unlike most other profiles here). LG's launch command uses `-fa on -sm row -c 262144 --no-context-shift`; `-sm row` (row split) instead of layer split can be more stable on multi-GPU with this hybrid attention; apply via the Expert panel / extra args if needed. Vision needs the separate mmproj file (mmproj-EXAONE-4.5-*.gguf). Integrated MTP/NextN layers exist in the GGUF but are NOT executed by llama.cpp (b9500), so no draft-mtp; draftless ngram-mod is used instead. presence_penalty is set to 0.0 instead of LG's official 1.5 because 1.5 causes loops in tool calling / structured output; for pure chat without tools: `-- --presence-penalty 1.5`.
profile_notes.frankenmerger.yaml: Merges often have inconsistent context limits and sampling sweet spots. The chat profile is optimised for roleplay/creative writing (higher temperature, stronger repeat penalty against loops in long RP sessions). The coding profile is defensive: these models are not primarily trained for code; if code performance is poor, prefer a dedicated coder profile.
profile_notes.gemma-3.yaml: Google's Gemma 3 family. The 1B model is text-only with 32k context; 4B/12B/27B support text and image input with 128k context. AutoTuner uses the GGUF context metadata to distinguish the 1B limit and attaches a matching sibling mmproj when present. Official instruction-tuned sampling is temp 1.0, top_k 64, top_p 0.95, with repetition penalty left at 1.0.
profile_notes.gemma-3n.yaml: Gemma 3n E2B/E4B has a native 32k context and official temp 1.0, top_k 64, top_p 0.95 sampling. llama.cpp b10760 supports its text and vision paths, but the MTMD code still intentionally skips Gemma 3n audio tensors; do not present a current stock build as local audio-capable. A matching sibling mmproj is attached automatically when available.
profile_notes.gemma-4.yaml: Gemma is sensitive to repeat_penalty > 1.0. Multimodality by size: E2B/E4B = text+image+audio, 12B = text+image+audio (NEW "Unified" variant: encoder-free, vision/audio through direct linear projections instead of separate encoders), 26B-A4B + 31B = text+image. Context: E2B/E4B = 128k, 12B/26B-A4B/31B = 256k. Architecture note: the 12B language-model GGUF loads under general.architecture "gemma4" (identical to the rest of the family); the strings gemma4uv/gemma4ua are only projector types on the separate mmproj file. Scanner, KV logic, and match_profile therefore treat the 12B like any other Gemma 4 model. Thinking mode can be enabled with <|think|> at the start of the system prompt. The coding profile uses temp=1.5 (vs. 1.0 chat) following community tests showing that Gemma 4 produces more creative and more correct coding solutions at a higher temperature; override with `-- --temp 1.0` if the higher temperature disturbs your workflow. The sampler order is set explicitly through extra_args as "temperature;top_p;top_k" (Gemma 4 recommendation; see the comment above), which matters because the default sampler chain would otherwise distort the high coding temperature.
profile_notes.glm-4_7.yaml: Flagship 358B MoE coding model or the 30B Flash variant. Three-level thinking architecture (interleaved / preserved / turn-level thinking). Very strong in SWE-Bench (~73.8% for the full model, 59.2% for Flash) and tool use. The chat profile is Z.ai's official "general evaluation" recommendation (temp 1.0). The coding profile is more deterministic (0.6) for stable tool calls and reproducible code output. Note: GLM-5.1 (Z.ai's newest coding model, 256k context) now exists as well and will eventually need its own profile. Tip: set `thinking=enabled` for coding; internal reasoning traces noticeably improve code quality.
profile_notes.glm-5.yaml: Z.ai GLM-5/5.1 is a 744B-A40B MoE family for agentic coding and reasoning, with roughly 200k native context. Official chat sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95; coding uses the established deterministic temp 0.6 local profile. --jinja and preserved reasoning are important for long tool workflows. GLM-5.2 is intentionally separate because it adds a 1M context, glm-dsa/IndexShare attention, an improved MTP layer, and a newer minimum llama.cpp build.
profile_notes.glm-5_2.yaml: Z.ai GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 (non-Flash) share the glm-dsa GGUF architecture, native 1M context, IndexShare sparse attention, and one NextN/MTP layer, so they intentionally share this profile. GLM-5.3 keeps the official generation config temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95 and adds low/high/max reasoning effort in its embedded template (max by default); min_p=0.01 and top_k=40 retain the established local profile. Use llama.cpp b10174 or newer for the complete GLM DSA/MTP path, with current builds strongly preferred for indexer/backend fixes. Datacenter scale: even low-bit quants need hundreds of GB, so a 48 GB workstation requires substantial RAM/CPU expert offload and cannot exploit a 1M cache. GLM-5.3-Flash is intentionally separate: it is a 320B-A18B multimodal KDA/DSA hybrid with the new glm5next architecture.
profile_notes.glm-5_3_flash.yaml: Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash is a natively multimodal 320B-A18B MoE with 45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention layers plus 11 pooled DSA/MLA layers, mHC residual streams, 288 routed experts (top-8) + 1 shared expert, one NextN/MTP layer, and native 1M context. Official sampling is temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95; the embedded template supports low/high/max reasoning effort and defaults to max. IMPORTANT: as of 2026-08-30, glm5next support is still in open upstream llama.cpp PRs #27752 (text + experimental MTP) and #27773 (text + vision); stock mainline does not load the architecture yet. Use a matching patched build and GGUF conversion. The implementations have different current trade-offs: one omits vision, the other keeps MTP for a separate PR, and multiple sequences require unified KV handling. Published Unsloth GGUFs use general.architecture=glm5next and offer separate mmproj files. Prefer IQ3 or higher: real Metal/CPU testing reported repeated-token failure for UD-IQ1_M while IQ3_XXS and IQ4_XS remained coherent. Current development CUDA also has a reported DSA-pool ceiling near 262k context, so AutoTuner caps this preview profile at 262,140 despite the model's native 1M metadata. Raise that cap only after the selected runtime fixes and validates the full window.
profile_notes.glm-ocr.yaml: Z.ai GLM-OCR: a 0.9B document OCR model (CogViT encoder, GLM-0.5B decoder with a native MTP head). Decoding is deterministic as published (do_sample false); a repetition penalty would damage tables and repeated characters. Official task prompts are "Text Recognition:", "Formula Recognition:" and "Table Recognition:". AutoTuner attaches a compatible sibling mmproj when present. This exposes element recognition through llama-server; it does not reproduce the separate PP-DocLayout page-layout stage of the full pipeline.
profile_notes.gpt-oss.yaml: OpenAI gpt-oss (20B: 21B total / 3.6B active; 120B: 117B / 5.1B active), architecture "gpt-oss", native MXFP4 MoE (in llama.cpp mainline). The 20B runs in 16 GB VRAM. MUST be run with the harmony format: `--jinja` is mandatory here, otherwise the output is garbled. Sampling is deliberately unusual (temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0 / NO top_k / NO repeat_penalty): top_k and penalties truncate or break the harmony control tokens and destroy the chain-of-thought. Reasoning effort is NOT controlled by a sampler but through the system prompt ("Reasoning: low|medium|high"); in the AutoTuner GUI it can be set per model as reasoning_effort (low/medium/high), which llama-server passes through via `--chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"high"}'`. The full chain-of-thought is visible through the API but, according to OpenAI, NOT intended for end users. Native tool/function-calling capabilities are present. Quant levels change almost nothing about the file size of the MXFP4 MoE: the experts are always MXFP4; q8_0/F16 only affect embeddings/attention.
profile_notes.granite-4_1.yaml: Dense decoder-only Transformer (3B/8B/30B), not a reasoning model. Strong in tool calling, instruction following, RAG, and coding. The 3B checkpoint supports 128k context; 8B and 30B support up to 512k. Granite Switch 4.1 is intentionally separate because it uses the dedicated graniteswitch architecture and requires a newer llama.cpp build. Apache 2.0 license. Do not use CUDA 13.2 because it can produce gibberish; this warning does not affect Vulkan on AMD.
profile_notes.granite-4_2.yaml: IBM Granite 4.2 is a dense 3B/8B/30B reasoning family with default full thinking, optional non-thinking and low-effort modes, reasoning-augmented tool calling, coding, and multilingual chat. The embedded Jinja template accepts enable_thinking, low_effort, and reasoning_effort=low; AutoTuner's Expert reasoning controls can pass the matching template kwargs. All three checkpoints are natively 128k. IBM advertises a 512k long-context extension only for 30B, while its published serving commands and checkpoint config use 131,072; this profile therefore keeps the safe native limit. Apache 2.0.
profile_notes.granite-embedding-r2.yaml: IBM Granite Embedding Multilingual R2 (April 2026): ModernBERT-based dense embedding models, architecture "modern-bert". Two sizes: 97m (384-dim) and 311m (768-dim, Matryoshka 768->512/384/256/128). 200+ languages (extended for 52 + code), 32768-token context, CLS pooling, Apache 2.0. NO chat/completion: run it as an embedding endpoint (--embeddings and --pooling cls are set in extra_args). Use cases: semantic search, RAG retrieval. The reranker is a separate model. NOTE: if AutoTuner GUI logic (sampling dropdowns, draft/n-gram checkboxes, KV quant) remains visible for this profile, simply ignore it; in --embeddings mode it has no effect. Should a future AutoTuner build gain an explicit "embedding" task switch, this profile can be simplified accordingly.
profile_notes.granite-switch-4_1.yaml: IBM Granite Switch 4.1 uses embedded adapters selected by control tokens for RAG, safety, and explainability workloads. It has a dedicated graniteswitch GGUF architecture and 128k context. Use llama.cpp b10342 or newer. Chat keeps modest variation; coding/tool workflows use IBM-style greedy decoding. Apache 2.0 license.
profile_notes.grok.yaml: xAI Grok-2: large MoE, open weights, architecture "grok" (in llama.cpp mainline). Native context up to 131072. xAI gives no prominent llama.cpp sampler recommendation, so conservative defaults are used (temp 0.7 chat / 0.3 coding); adjust if needed. Datacenter/cluster class (several hundred GB depending on quant); on a single workstation only with a lot of RAM plus --n-cpu-moe.
profile_notes.hunyuan-moe.yaml: Tencent Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct: fine-grained MoE, 80B total / 13B active, architecture "hunyuan_moe" (NOT "hunyuan-dense"!). Hybrid reasoning (fast/slow thinking, dynamic CoT depth), native 256k context. Sampling uses Tencent's official CHAT values temp=0.7 / top_k=20 / top_p=0.8 / rep=1.05, deliberately separated from the Hunyuan-MT translator profile (top_p 0.6), which would be wrong for an A13B chat model. --jinja is mandatory. With 13B active parameters it runs well on a 32 GB card plus --n-cpu-moe. Note: some early GGUF quants had a broken, very high perplexity; prefer verified quants (for example Unsloth Dynamic).
profile_notes.hunyuan.yaml: Tencent Hunyuan-MT (HY-MT2-7B): dense 7B translation model, architecture "hunyuan-dense" (supported in llama.cpp mainline, no mmproj, no hybrid). The sampling defaults are Tencent's official Hunyuan-MT values (temp 0.7 / top_p 0.6 / top_k 20 / rep 1.05), deliberately different from the usual chat profiles because the model is trained for translation rather than free writing. NOTE: should this profile later also catch generic Hunyuan CHAT models (for example Hunyuan-A13B), temp 1.0 would be more appropriate there; create a separate profile with a more specific pattern in that case. general.name shows a checkpoint name ("Global_Step_560") for this GGUF; that is cosmetic and does not affect loading.
profile_notes.hy-mt2.yaml: Tencent Hy-MT2 (May 2026): "fast-thinking" translation family (33 languages): 1.8B / 7B dense, 30B-A3B MoE (30B total / 3B active). The architecture is NEW: general.architecture "hy_v3", not compatible with the old Hunyuan-MT profile (hunyuan-dense) or A13B (hunyuan_moe). Since llama.cpp b9993 (PR #25395) hy_v3 including MTP support is part of mainline. The 1.8B/7B GGUFs with architecture "hunyuan-dense" already ran before that. Sampling uses the official Tencent values temp=0.7 / top_p=1.0 / top_k off / rep=1.0, deliberately different from the old Hunyuan-MT (top_p 0.6). Coding mode is greedy (temp 0) for reproducible, literal translations. Pure translation model, not a chat/coding LLM. Note from the GGUF repository (litigerking): with llama-cli you may need -r '<eos:6124c78e>' as a reverse prompt for clean EOS handling; not needed for the tuner's llama-server path.
profile_notes.hy4-preview.yaml: Tencent Hy4 Preview (August 2026): 770B total / 49B active MoE, 78 layers, 256 routed experts + 1 shared expert, top-8 routing, Gated DSA/IndexCache, iHC residual streams, and native 1M context. Official sampling is temp=0.9, top_p=1.0, top_k disabled; reasoning defaults to high and can be changed by the embedded chat template's reasoning_effort parameter. IMPORTANT: stock upstream llama.cpp b10839 supports the separate "hy_v4" format, not these "hyv4" GGUFs. AngelSlim/Hy4-preview-GGUF documents a community patch based on llama.cpp commit 0cea36222; both published GGUFs require that architecture patch. Their Q4_K_M is about 435 GiB and STQ1_0 about 214 GiB at full residency, so practical use needs datacenter-class aggregate VRAM or very large RAM with expert offload. The community conversion drops Hy4's native MTP layer, therefore its GGUF cannot use embedded speculative decoding.
profile_notes.kimi-k2.yaml: Moonshot Kimi-K2: 1T total / 32B active MoE with MLA, architecture "deepseek2" (DeepSeek-V3-like). Therefore NO arch_fallback: it would otherwise also catch DeepSeek-V3/V3.2 and GLM-4.7-Flash; matching only through the filename "kimi". Variants: K2-Instruct(-0905, text), K2.5/K2.6 (vision via mmproj, merged in mainline), K2.7-Code. Sampling: chat = Moonshot/Unsloth temp=0.6 / min_p=0.01 (against repetition); coding = thinking defaults temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95 (K2.5+/K2.7 use thinking; "instant" is not supported there). --jinja is mandatory (tool calls). Datacenter class: Q2 ~250-380 GB, Q4 ~620 GB; a cluster or a workstation with a very large amount of RAM. Note: some ubergarm/ik quants need the ik_llama.cpp fork; the standard Unsloth/bartowski quants run on mainline.
profile_notes.kimi-k3.yaml: Moonshot Kimi-K3 is a native-multimodal 2.8T-A104B MoE with KDA, Attention Residuals, 896 experts (16 active), and 1M context. llama.cpp b10448 added the dedicated kimi-k3 TEXT loader and converter; its converter deliberately skips vision_tower/mm_projector tensors, so current mainline support must not be presented as local K3 vision support. K3 cannot be routed through the older kimi-linear or Kimi-K2/deepseek2 loaders. Official settings use temp 1.0 with top_p 0.95 for single-step work and 1.0 for agentic tasks. The profile requires b10749 because that is the first tagged build with corrected no-scan SSM state tensors for Kimi-K3/Kimi-Linear. Thinking stays enabled and complete reasoning/tool-call history is preserved. At this scale it remains a cluster or very-high-RAM model, not a practical 48 GB workstation checkpoint.
profile_notes.kimi-linear.yaml: Moonshot's 48B-A3B hybrid model uses three KDA layers for every global MLA layer and supports a 1M context with a much smaller recurrent-state footprint. Mainline architecture support began at b7957, but b10749 is required here for the corrected no-scan treatment of Kimi Linear SSM state tensors; older builds can silently use the wrong allocation/lifetime contract. This profile is separate from Kimi-K2 (deepseek2) and Kimi-K3 (kimi-k3). The official model card does not prescribe temperature/top-k/top-p, so embedded GGUF sampling metadata remains authoritative when present.
profile_notes.laguna-s-2_1.yaml: Laguna S 2.1 (Poolside) is a text-only 117.6B-A8.5B MoE built for long-horizon agentic coding, terminal work, tool use, and preserved interleaved reasoning. Use llama.cpp b10087 or newer for the Unsloth GGUF; for sharded Unsloth quants select only shard 00001 and llama.cpp loads the remaining shards automatically. The native context is 1M; GGUF metadata already carries YaRN factor 128 with original context 8192, so no manual RoPE override is required. Thinking is enabled by the embedded template by default. For quick replies it can be disabled per request with chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking":false}. Keep reasoning history for coding agents. Optional official Laguna-S-2.1-DFlash-BF16.gguf (~2.2 GB) enables DFlash speculation; leave it unassigned if VRAM pressure or Vulkan benchmarks show no speedup.
profile_notes.laguna-xs-2_1.yaml: Laguna XS 2.1 (Poolside) is a text-only 33B-A3B MoE for agentic coding and long-horizon work with interleaved, preserved thinking and 262,144 tokens of context. Use llama.cpp b11598+ (PR #30331): XS 2.1 stores YaRN beta_fast 64, which older builds ignored in favour of 32. Thinking is on by default and can be disabled per request with enable_thinking. Poolside's DFlash speculator (Laguna-XS-2.1-DFlash, up to 7 draft tokens) pairs automatically when a GGUF of it is present. Official sampling: temperature 1.0, top-k 20, top-p 1.0. The predecessor Laguna XS.2 uses the same profile.
profile_notes.leanstral.yaml: Leanstral 1.5 (Mistral, 3 July 2026): Apache-2.0 Lean 4 code-agent and theorem-proving model. Sparse MoE: 119B total / 6.5B active (A6B), 128 experts, 4 active per token, MLA attention (DeepSeek style), 256k context, multimodal input (text+image; optionally load the matching mmproj file and assign it as mmproj in the GUI; without mmproj only the text path runs). Trained with CISPO RL in a multi-turn proof environment (Lean compiler feedback) and a code-agent environment (filesystem + Lean LSP). Saturates miniF2F, solves 587/672 PutnamBench, SOTA on FATE-H. Chat profile = high-reasoning/proof mode (temp 0.7), coding profile = deterministic code agent (temp 0.2). Set reasoning mode explicitly: -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"high"}'. NOTE on test-time scaling: Leanstral scales monotonically with the token budget (244 solved problems at 200k -> 587 at 4M on PutnamBench). For pass@k proof search (sampling many proof candidates) it pays to raise the temperature towards 1.0 to generate diverse proof paths; in chat mode via -- --temp 1.0. Vibe CLI (Mistral): vibe --agent lean.
profile_notes.lfm2.yaml: LiquidAI LFM2 / LFM2.5 edge family (short conv + GQA). Sampling follows LiquidAI's official recommendation (temp 0.3, min_p 0.15, rep 1.05): small models, hence a deliberately low temperature against incoherence.
