IMPORTANT (LFM2.5-Audio): this is an audio-in/audio-out speech model. This profile only provides sensible text-side defaults; the actual audio pipeline (audio encoder/decoder) runs through the dedicated llama.cpp audio paths, not through the plain text chat server. Loaded as a text chat model it works but produces no speech. LFM2 is technically a conv/attention hybrid; for this 1.5B model the tuner's KV-cache overestimate is negligible (tiny model).
profile_notes.ling-3.yaml: InclusionAI Ling 3.0 uses the bailingmoe3 hybrid KDA/MLA MoE architecture. Flash is 124B-A5.1B with 256k context; Tiny is the smaller 7.9B-A1.3B sibling. Official sampling is temp 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 with thinking enabled. llama.cpp b10460 added conversion, inference, integrated and separate NEXTN/MTP support; this profile requires b10749 because that is the first tagged build with corrected no-scan BailingMoE3 SSM state tensors. Compatible MTP weights can use up to three speculative tokens. Do not route these checkpoints through the older Ling 2.6 bailingmoe2.5/bailing_hybrid fork profile. llama.cpp b11063 (PR #28682) adds a dedicated Ling 3.0 (Bailing V3) chat parser that llama-server selects automatically with --jinja from the template's <role> markers: a tool call emitted before </think> (the template pre-opens the think block) now surfaces as tool_calls instead of being swallowed into reasoning_content. Older builds load the model but can lose such tool calls in thinking mode, so b11063+ is recommended for tool use.
profile_notes.ling-ring.yaml: InclusionAI (Ant Group) Ling / Ring 2.x: MoE family, architecture "bailingmoe2" (mainline via PR #16063). Ling = instruct/general, Ring = reasoning (derived from Ling, <think> chains). Sizes: Ling/Ring-mini-2.0 (~17B / 1.4B active, runs well locally), -flash, and the 1T flagships (Ling-2.5-1T / Ring-1T, 1T total / ~63B active, hybrid linear attention, up to 1M context; pure datacenter/cluster models, Q4 ~500 GB). Sampling follows the InclusionAI recommendation temp=0.7 / top_p=0.8 / rep=1.05; coding is more deterministic. --jinja for template/reasoning. IMPORTANT: Ling-2.6-flash uses the newer "bailingmoe2.5" and does NOT run on vanilla llama.cpp; use bailingmoe2-5.yaml (fork) for it.
profile_notes.llama-3.yaml: Standard profile for Meta's Llama 3 series. Llama 3.1+ natively supports 128k context; older and smaller variants are limited to their real limit through GGUF metadata. Llama 4 has its own profile because of its different official sampling and 1M/10M context limits. Chat is the all-round default; coding is strongly deterministic.
profile_notes.llama-4.yaml: Meta's multimodal Llama 4 MoE family. Official Instruct limits are 10M for Scout and 1M for Maverick; base checkpoints are 256k. AutoTuner always caps this family maximum with each GGUF's native context metadata and the actual RAM/VRAM budget, so Maverick is never promoted to Scout's limit. Official reference generation defaults are temp 0.6 / top_p 0.9. Image input needs a matching mmproj; llama.cpp b10760 still warns that Llama 4 vision quality is known to be degraded, so validate vision-critical workloads independently.
profile_notes.llm-jp-4_1.yaml: LLM-jp-4.1 thinking models from Japan's National Institute of Informatics (8B and 33B dense, 32B-A3B MoE; Japanese/English, 65,536 context). They use an OpenAI-Harmony-compatible template with their own tokenizer; llama.cpp b11320+ ships the matching llm-jp-harmony-v1 handler, so --jinja separates reasoning from content and parses single and parallel tool calls. Older builds fail chat parsing. Sampling follows the NII cookbook (temp 0.7 / top_p 0.9, no top_k, no repetition penalty). Reasoning effort is selected through the template (reasoning_effort low/medium/high). LLM-jp-4.0 has no handler marker and is not covered.
profile_notes.maple.yaml: DeepGrove Maple-Preview is a 20B-A1B ternary-weight reasoning MoE: 24 layers, 256 experts with 8 active, 3:1 sliding-window (512) to global attention, 131,072 native context, MIT license. The official GGUFs pack the ternary weights as TQ1_0 or TQ2_0 with a Q4_K or F16 LM head (4.6 to 5.9 GiB). llama.cpp b10964 (PR #27000, also stable v0.4.1) added the maple architecture; this profile requires that build. Vulkan has TQ1_0/TQ2_0 matmul kernels, so the whole model runs on the GPU there; CUDA/HIP have no ternary kernels, so on HIP llama.cpp keeps the TQ expert tensors in host memory and computes them on the CPU. DeepGrove publishes no generation_config, so the sampling defaults are the usual thinking-model values (temp 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20). The preview is tuned for raw reasoning and received little agentic post-training; thinking is on by default via the embedded ChatML-style template.
profile_notes.mellum.yaml: JetBrains Mellum2-12B-A2.5B: sparse MoE (64 experts, 8 active), 12B total / 2.5B active, 128k context via layer-selective YaRN, Apache 2.0. No multimodality. Inference cost/speed behaves like a dense 2.5B despite the 12B total size. Three variants: Base (completion), Instruct (direct), Thinking (<think> CoT). For the Thinking variant set `--jinja` as an extra arg so that <think> blocks are cleanly separated into the reasoning_content field: -- --jinja. ngram_method is DELIBERATELY set to ngram-map-k4v here (not the global default ngram-mod): it is MTP-compatible and survives both cases, whether or not llama.cpp recognises/executes the MTP head JetBrains describes. On crashes with speculation: disable draft/n-gram in the GUI and compare tok/s (a MoE A2.5B does not benefit from speculation for certain).
profile_notes.microsoft_phi-4-3_5.yaml: Small but extremely capable model. Runs most stably with greedy decoding (temp 0) for logical tasks, which is therefore the coding default. Chat mode allows some variation (temp 0.5) but stays clearly more conservative than with larger models because Phi hallucinates faster at high temperature than 30B+ models.
profile_notes.minicpm5.yaml: OpenBMB MiniCPM5-1B: dense 1B on-device model (standard llama architecture, no hybrid, no mmproj), Apache-2.0, 1B-class SOTA for tool use/code/reasoning, native 128k context. Architecture "llama", therefore NO arch_fallback (it would otherwise catch all Llama models); matching only by filename. Hybrid reasoning from one checkpoint: think/no-think through the chat template (enable_thinking). Sampling follows the OpenBMB recommendation: chat = no-think (temp 0.7), coding = think (temp 0.9), top_p 0.95 in both. --jinja is mandatory (chat template + XML tool-call parsing). For tool calling, SGLang/llama.cpp with the correct parser is recommended.
profile_notes.minicpm-v-4_7.yaml: OpenBMB MiniCPM-V 4.7 (1B dense and 35B-A3B MoE on Qwen3.5-style backbones, 262,144 tokens of context): image and video understanding. Image input needs llama.cpp b11551+ (PR #29416) for the minicpmv4_7 projector; text works on older builds. The official GGUF projector is named generically (mmproj-model-f16.gguf), so attach it by hand if AutoTuner does not pair it. DSpark drafters (dspark-MiniCPM-V-4_7-*) are listed but not selected by default: on b12187 (R9700 + RX 9070 XT) the 35B-A3B drafter sped up code on Vulkan (118 to 160 tok/s with 7 draft tokens) but slowed German prose and every HIP run (for example 119 to 42-73 tok/s), so select it per model when it pays off. Official instruct sampling: temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, top-k 100, repetition penalty 1.03; thinking can be switched per request with enable_thinking.
profile_notes.minimax-01.yaml: MiniMax-Text-01 is a 456B-A45.9B MoE hybrid with Lightning Attention recurrent layers and one full-attention layer per eight blocks; MiniMax-M1 uses the same llama.cpp minimax-01 architecture. Native support landed in llama.cpp b10437. AutoTuner counts recurrent-layer boolean arrays, sizes KV only for full-attention layers, and uses expert-aware placement. The model is far larger than ordinary laptop memory even when quantized; small local systems require a heavily quantized split and substantial system RAM.
profile_notes.minimax-m2.yaml: MiniMax-M2 is a sparse-MoE model (154 experts, 8 active) tuned for agentic coding and tool use. Native context is 192k (clamped to GGUF native). The build in the tree is the REAP-pruned 139B-A10B variant — same arch tag and sampler recommendation as the full model, just fewer experts, so it shares this profile. Recommended samplers (temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 40) follow MiniMaxAI's published defaults; min_p 0.02 trims the routing tail to curb repetition on the pruned weights. As a large MoE it relies on AutoTuner's capacity-fill spread to pack both GPUs with expert layers; everything else (n-cpu-moe, tensor-split, ctx) is derived automatically.
profile_notes.minimax-m3.yaml: MiniMax-M3 is a native multimodal 428B-A23B MoE with MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) and 1M context. Use llama.cpp b10142 or newer for the text, MSA, vision, and specialized tool-call path. Vision additionally requires an M3 mmproj. Use an MSA-aware GGUF conversion that retains every blk.N.index_q_proj/index_k_proj tensor; older dense-fallback GGUFs are not equivalent. Flash Attention is required for the intended sparse path; unsupported no-FA/unified-KV multi-sequence modes can fall back to dense attention and lose the 1M-context efficiency. Released weights do not contain the advertised MTP modules, so AutoTuner keeps conservative draftless speculation. Official sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95; other sampler fields are inherited from GGUF metadata.
profile_notes.ministral.yaml: Ministral 3 (3B/8B/14B), Mistral's edge family, all with vision (mmproj). The 14B Reasoning variant is comparable to Mistral Small 3.2 24B in reasoning benchmarks (85% AIME '25). The architecture shares RoPE scaling with Devstral Small 2 / Llama 4. Apache 2.0. Chat profile = Reasoning variant (temp 1.0, Mistral recommendation). The coding profile also suits the Instruct variants (temp ~0.1). Note: the pattern matches all variants; for Instruct models simply use coding mode for chat as well, or override via CLI: -- --temp 0.0
profile_notes.mistral-medium.yaml: Mistral Medium 3.5 (128B dense, multimodal text+image, 29 April 2026) is Mistral's first unified model, replacing Medium 3.1, Magistral AND Devstral 2 in one (Mistral itself: "supersedes all our previous coding models, namely Devstral, across all benchmarks"). Hybrid reasoning with per-request configurable reasoning_effort (none/high). Modified MIT License. Vibe CLI (Mistral's coding agent) now runs on Medium 3.5 instead of Devstral 2. Locally: ~64 GB RAM for UD-Q4_K_XL via llama.cpp. Chat profile = Mistral's default (temp 0.7, works for both reasoning modes). Coding profile = more deterministic (temp 0.2) for agentic code tasks. Enable reasoning mode via: -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"high"}'. IMPORTANT: use GGUFs from 1 May 2026 or newer; earlier versions had a YaRN bug (mscale_all_dim) that ruined long-context performance (Mistral itself confirmed that the original Transformers config had a long-context performance bug). At Unsloth the fixed build is called, for example, UD-Q4_K_XL.
profile_notes.mistral-small-3.yaml: Dense 24B Mistral Small 3.1/3.2 instruction models with 128k context and Pixtral vision. Mistral recommends temperature 0.15 and a tailored system prompt. Current llama.cpp uses the mistral3 text architecture and requires a matching mmproj for image input; for Mistral Small 3.1 MTMD recommends the mistral-v7 chat template when a converted checkpoint does not embed it.
profile_notes.mimo-v2_6.yaml: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6 Flash/Pro RL uses the existing mimo2 MoE architecture. llama.cpp b11102+ (PR #29257) adds MXFP4 expert conversion and correct Jinja tool-parser selection; older builds can select the wrong Qwen3-Coder parser. Official sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 for chat and coding. The 1,048,576 context ceiling is clamped to the GGUF and available memory; it is not a promise that 1M fits locally. Text and vision use llama-server plus the matching mmproj; the audio decoder is excluded by the converter, so this is not a speech-output profile. MTP depends on actual GGUF head tensors, not the model card alone. A separate MTP head from the converter's --mtp export (b11195+) needs llama.cpp b11195+ (PR #29294). No local V2.6 weights were available for this audit; profile, build gate and KV planning have unit coverage.
profile_notes.mimo-v2_6-distill.yaml: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B is a supervised fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B on MiMo-V2.6-generated data for coding, agent tasks, visual coding and cybersecurity (qwen35 architecture, 262,144 context, Qwen3.5 mmproj for images). It is not the MiMo-V2.6 Flash/Pro MoE, so it gets its own profile: official sampling is temp 0.6 / top_k 20 / top_p 0.95 for chat and coding. Thinking is on by default (chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false turns it off); the MiMo v2.6 template keeps reasoning history and emits Qwen3-Coder-style XML tool calls, which --jinja parses. No MTP head is included, so only draftless n-gram speculation applies.
profile_notes.fastcontext-1_0-4b.yaml: Microsoft FastContext 1.0 4B SFT/RL is a Qwen3-based repository explorer, not a general coding agent. Both local GGUFs declare 262,144 context and sampling temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8 / top_k 20; this profile follows those artifact defaults. The planner still clamps context to available memory. Use the embedded Jinja template and provide repository-search tools in the client; AutoTuner does not grant filesystem access or run those tools. No qwen3 architecture fallback is used, so unrelated Qwen3 models retain their own settings. The 30B FastContext variant is not covered here.
profile_notes.xing-4_0.yaml: Xing 4.0 29B-A4B (formerly TeleChat; xing4_0 architecture: MLA attention, manifold-constrained hyper-connections, 64 experts with 4 active, one MTP layer, 256K context). Mainline llama.cpp loads it since b12156 (PR #31589). AutoTuner uses the embedded MTP head with one draft token and no confidence gate (p-min 0): measured on b12187 (IQ4_NL, R9700) 90-92 tok/s against 82 without MTP on Vulkan and 74-77 against 64.5 on HIP; the usual p-min 0.75 gate removed most of the gain, longer drafts were slower. Sampling from the model card: chat temperature 1.0, coding 0.8, top-p 0.95, repetition penalty 1.05. Thinking is on by default and can be switched off through the chat template (enable_thinking).
profile_notes.voxcpm2.yaml: VoxCPM2 BaseLM is recognized so it does not silently receive generic chat settings. It belongs to Voice Lab's separate TTS pipeline and cannot synthesize speech through AutoTuner's ordinary chat-server path. Use building llama.cpp/voicelab_voxcpm2_vulkan_build.ps1 for the isolated tc-mb/llama.cpp-omni build (voxcpm2-cli and llama-tts-server) and supply the complete TTS assets there. No minicpm4 architecture-wide block is applied to unrelated language models.
profile_notes.muse-glimmer.yaml: Meta Muse Glimmer 30B is a dense multimodal local-agent model with a separate perception mmproj, 131k context, interleaved reasoning/tool use, and an optional DFlash block drafter. It requires llama.cpp b10353 or newer. Official sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 64 in both chat and agentic coding. Keep reasoning history for multi-turn tool workflows. Reasoning strength is controlled in the system prompt with "Reasoning strength: low|medium|high|xhigh". The Q4 model plus mmproj, KV cache, and drafter targets a 24-32 GB device; on this dual-AMD system benchmark the optional drafter because Vulkan overhead can offset gains. For tool use, b11100+ is recommended: PR #29242 fixes a tool call emitted as the first generated text being misclassified as content rather than tool_calls. --jinja selects the corrected parser automatically; the loader minimum remains b10353. Structured output (response_format json_schema) needs b11249+: PR #29615 makes the --jinja parser enforce the schema, which older builds ignored.
profile_notes.nanbeige-4_2.yaml: Compact 3B non-embedding-parameter looped Transformer for reasoning, coding, agents, and XML tool calls. The model card advertises 262,144 context and recommends temp 0.6/top-p 0.95/top-k 20 for reasoning and temp 1.0 for agent use. Preserved thinking is useful for multi-turn tools; disable it manually when minimizing KV history matters more than continuity.
profile_notes.nemotron-3-nano-omni.yaml: Hybrid Mamba2-Transformer MoE, 30B total / ~3B active. Multimodal: text + image + audio + video (via mmproj). Reasoning variant with native <think>/</think> tokens (12/13). Chat profile = NVIDIA's official reasoning recommendation (temp 0.6). The coding profile is more deterministic (temp 0.2) for stable code output. CAUTION: do NOT use with CUDA 13.2; it produces gibberish output. NVIDIA is working on a fix; until then use CUDA 12.9 or 13.0. Tip: to force or disable thinking explicitly, append at start: -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true}' or -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
profile_notes.nemotron-3-puzzle.yaml: Text-only 75.3B-total/9.3B-active compression of Nemotron 3 Super with the same 88-block Mamba-2/latent-MoE/attention layout, integrated multi-token prediction, and up to 1,048,576 context (262,144 default). Puzzle prunes expert channels per layer (expert FFN widths 1280-2688), routes 4 to 18 experts depending on the layer, and shrinks the Mamba state from 128 to 96 channels. The profile requires llama.cpp b10786 because that build first reads the per-layer expert arrays; AutoTuner refuses older binaries before launch instead of letting tensor creation abort. Sampling, thinking control, and MTP settings follow the Super profile. On HIP, llama.cpp b11249+ (PR #28717) runs the 96-channel Mamba-2 scan on the GPU; Vulkan and older HIP builds only have 128/256-channel scan kernels and schedule that operation on the CPU in every Mamba layer, so prefer HIP b11249+.
profile_notes.nemotron-3-super.yaml: Text-only 120B-total/12B-active Mamba-2 + latent-MoE + attention hybrid (88 blocks: 40 Mamba, 40 MoE, 8 attention) with integrated multi-token prediction and up to 1,048,576 context; NVIDIA deploys 262,144 by default. Official sampling is temp 1.0/top-p 0.95 for every task. Thinking is controlled through the chat template (enable_thinking, low_effort, and a reasoning budget), which AutoTuner drives with its reasoning dropdown and --reasoning-budget. The profile enables the integrated MTP head with three draft tokens as NVIDIA recommends and keeps MTP-compatible n-gram speculation. At roughly 60 GB in Q4 this is a two-GPU or CPU-expert-offload workstation model, not a 16 GB single-card checkpoint.
profile_notes.nemotron-3_5.yaml: Text-only 30B-total/3B-active Mamba-2 + attention + MoE hybrid with one integrated MTP layer and up to 1,048,576 context. NVIDIA's official sampling is temp 1.0/top-p 0.95. Mainline b10665 adds its DSpark sidecar contract; AutoTuner uses n-max 7 and p-min 0.0 so confidence-head-free releases do not abort. The official local llama.cpp example starts around 40,960 context; larger windows remain subject to measured KV/recurrent/runtime capacity.
profile_notes.nemotron-3_5-bolt.yaml: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: a 74B-total/9B-active compression of Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (nemotron_h_moe, 88 blocks, 240-496 experts per layer, 9 active) with image input and up to 262,144 tokens of context. Needs llama.cpp b11668+ (PR #30520, first release b11669): older builds create the expert tensors with the wrong shape and abort. The mmproj uses the nemotron_omni projector. NVIDIA's llama.cpp recipes pair the model with its LiLiCorr drafter (draft-dflash, 6-7 draft tokens, q8_0 KV for the 28 GB recipe); AutoTuner lists a paired DFlash/LiLiCorr draft but does not select it by default: on 48 GB of VRAM (b12187) the draft and its rollback state cut the planned context from 168K/262K to 16K/24K tokens for +7 % decode on Vulkan and -25 % on HIP. Sampling: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95. Thinking is controlled through the chat template (enable_thinking).
profile_notes.nemotron-3_5-super-vl.yaml: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: a 120B-total/12B-active Mamba-2 + latent-MoE + attention hybrid (nemotron_h_moe, 88 blocks, 512 experts with 22 active) with a C-RADIO image/video encoder and up to 1,048,576 tokens of context. Needs llama.cpp b11668+ (PR #30520, first release b11669); the mmproj uses the nemotron_omni projector, which older builds cannot load. The MTP head ships as a separate mtp-*.gguf and is paired automatically (three draft tokens as NVIDIA serves it); ggml-org also publishes a LiLiCorr drafter. Official sampling: temperature 1.0 / top-p 0.95 for text, 0.6 / 0.95 for vision tasks. Thinking is controlled through the chat template (enable_thinking). At roughly 65 GB in Q4 this is a two-GPU or CPU-expert-offload model.
profile_notes.ornith-1_5.yaml: Ornith 1.5 is a Qwen3.5-based reasoning/tool-calling family with 256k native context and validated YaRN extension to about 1M. Official general sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 (presence 1.5), while precise coding uses temp 0.6 and presence 0.0. AutoTuner keeps presence at 0.0 in both modes so OpenAI-style tool JSON remains stable; pure chat users can override it to 1.5. Filename-only matching avoids stealing opaque qwen35/qwen35moe re-quants from the generic Qwen profile. The older Ornith 1.0 profile remains unchanged.
profile_notes.ornith.yaml: Ornith 1.0 (DeepReinforce, June 2026, MIT): self-improving model family for agentic coding, post-trained on a Qwen 3.5 base. The GGUF architecture is "qwen35" (9B/31B dense) or "qwen35moe" (35B-A3B / 397B-A17B MoE), exactly the Qwen3.5/3.6 hybrid family (GatedDeltaNet + full attention); the scanner counts the KV cache correctly through recurrent_layers. This profile matches only by the filename pattern ("ornith"); re-quants without "ornith" in the name correctly land at qwen3_5-3_6.yaml. Reasoning model: the answer opens with <think>...</think> by default. Set `--jinja` as an extra arg at start so that the <think> block is cleanly separated into the reasoning_content field and <tool_call> blocks are parsed as OpenAI-style tool_calls (Ornith is primarily a tool-calling agent): -- --jinja. Sampling: uniformly temp=0.6 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=20 for chat AND coding (Ornith recommendation); temp=1.0 is only the benchmark reproduction value (-- --temp 1.0). Unlike generic Qwen3.5 (chat temp=1.0), which is the reason for this separate profile despite the identical architecture. Tip: the 9B dense model is suitable as an external draft model (Path A) for the 35B MoE; the GGUFs themselves ship no integrated MTP head.
profile_notes.paddleocr-vl.yaml: Compact 0.9B multilingual document VLM (109 languages), supported by llama.cpp's paddleocr text architecture and MTMD projector path. Official element prompts are "OCR:", "Table Recognition:", "Formula Recognition:", and "Chart Recognition:"; generation is deterministic. AutoTuner attaches a compatible sibling mmproj when present. This exposes element recognition via llama-server; it does not reproduce PaddleOCR's separate full page-layout pipeline or post-processing stages.
profile_notes.qwen-agentworld.yaml: Alibaba Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B: the first language world model (CPT+SFT+RL on environment simulation across 7 domains: MCP/tool, search, terminal, SWE, Android, web, OS), Apache-2.0. NO separate architecture: it is Qwen3.5-35B-A3B further trained, general.architecture "qwen35moe" (hybrid GatedDeltaNet + attention, 256 experts / 8+1, native 262k context). Separate profile by filename pattern "agentworld" (NO arch_fallback, because the architecture is identical to regular Qwen3.5/3.6-A3B and a duplicate qwen35moe fallback would become order-dependent), because the AgentWorld sampling recommendation (temp=0.6 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=20 in BOTH modes) deliberately differs from the generic Qwen3.5 coder/chat settings (temp 1.0 thinking): a world model should simulate consistent, factual state transitions. Thinking mode by default (<think>), qwen3 reasoning parser, --jinja mandatory. Qwen advises >=128k context (on OOM quantise the KV cache instead of lowering context below 128k); recommended output length 32k. Domain-specific system prompts live in the GitHub repository (prompts/); AgentWorld as an environment simulator needs these system prompts to deliver meaningful observations. With 3B active plus --n-cpu-moe it runs well on a 32 GB card; it runs on mainline llama-server (no fork). Regular Qwen3.5/3.6 models remain covered by qwen3_5-3_6.yaml.
profile_notes.qwen2_5-3.yaml: Excellent all-round model. The coding profile runs at temp=0.2 (vs. 0.7 chat); the Coder variants can also be run at an even lower temperature (0.1). Selectable through the GUI mode. Also catches Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (architecture qwen3moe) and Qwen3-Coder-Next (architecture qwen3next) through the pattern "qwen3-coder". Both have 256k native context, hence max_context 262144 (previously wrongly capped at 131072). Qwen3-Coder-Next is a hybrid (Gated DeltaNet + gated attention) and needs a current llama.cpp version with the DeltaNet operators, present on b9310. Note: Qwen3-Coder-Instruct is a pure instruct model without thinking; Alibaba recommends temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8 for it (chat mode at 0.7/0.9 is close). For deterministic code editing use coding mode (temp 0.2).
profile_notes.qwen3-vl.yaml: Alibaba Qwen3-VL: vision-language models, dense (2B/4B/8B/32B) and MoE (30B-A3B / 235B-A22B), Instruct + Thinking, architecture "qwen3vl" or "qwen3vlmoe" (both in llama.cpp mainline). Needs an mmproj file for the vision encoder; assign it as mmproj in the GUI; without mmproj only the text path runs. Sampling distinguishes Instruct (chat: temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8) and Thinking (coding: temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95), analogous to Qwen3.5/3.6. presence_penalty is set to 0.0 instead of Qwen's 1.5 because 1.5 causes tool-calling loops; for pure image description without tools: `-- --presence-penalty 1.5`. Note: on Vulkan/ROCm it has been reported that Qwen3-VL does not fully utilise the GPU (~80%) and is somewhat slower than the plain Qwen3 text model (llama.cpp #16895); not a fault of this profile.
profile_notes.qwen3_5-3_6.yaml: Qwen3.5 (February 2026) and Qwen3.6 (April 2026) are thinking-by-default multimodal models with 256k native context (extendable to 1.01M via YaRN). The original Qwen3 has only 32k and is automatically limited through the GGUF native_context. The chat profile corresponds to the official thinking setup; the coding profile mirrors the official QwenClawBench setting (temp=0.6). presence_penalty is set to 0.0 here instead of the official Qwen recommendation of 1.5 because 1.5 reproducibly causes tool-calling loops (structured output needs repeated tokens, which a high presence_penalty punishes). For pure chat without tools: `-- --presence-penalty 1.5`. New in Qwen3.6: the `preserve_thinking` API flag keeps thinking content across multi-turn conversations for better agentic consistency. Tip: `--jinja` as an extra arg at start enables the clean separation of <think> blocks into the reasoning_content API field (instead of leaving them inline in content): -- --jinja
profile_notes.qwen3_8.yaml: Qwen3.8-27B is a dense native vision-language model with optional thinking; Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is a text-only MoE (2.4T total, 95B active) whose thinking mode cannot be disabled. Both use a 3:1 Gated DeltaNet/full-attention layout, preserve historical reasoning by default, and support reasoning_effort values xhigh (default), medium, and low. The profile therefore enables Jinja and preserved reasoning and uses the official thinking defaults in both AutoTuner modes. Only the 27B model supports non-thinking inference; when selecting it manually, use enable_thinking=false together with temp 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, min_p 0.0, presence_penalty 1.5, and repeat_penalty 1.0. Avoid that high presence penalty for repetitive tool-call JSON if it causes loops. Vision requires a matching 27B mmproj once a GGUF conversion publishes one. External Qwen3.8 DFlash2 sidecars require mainline b10658+ (older builds only have the 58-tensor DFlash graph). AutoTuner detects that mismatch before launch and derives n-max 7 from the sidecar's block_size=8 metadata. The 2.4T checkpoint is datacenter-scale and not realistically runnable on a workstation, even with aggressive quantization and CPU expert offload.
profile_notes.qwen3_8_flash_next.yaml: Dedicated profile for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUFs declaring qwen4exp. Mainline llama.cpp added the loader in b10660 and AutoTuner's QSA graph-memory safety contract was measured on b10666. AutoTuner requires b10737+ because the follow-up QSA sequence-copy, block-keying, multimodal-input, and CUDA-abort fixes in PR #27941 are required for correct serving. The model has 48 hybrid MoE blocks, 512 experts with 10 active, full attention every fourth block (12 normal KV layers), an additional QSA indexer cache, and 262,144 native context. Its PLE per-layer n-gram embedding table is a giant read-lazy host mapping rather than splittable layer weight; AutoTuner sizes the full file mapping separately from its active-row residency and defaults this profile to Safe/ubatch 64. Balanced/Throughput remain available at ubatch 128/256 because the QSA graph grows with context x ubatch. PLE is not advertised as generic draft-mtp.
profile_notes.seed-oss.yaml: ByteDance Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct: dense 36B reasoning/agentic model, Apache-2.0, native 512k context, architecture "seed_oss". Special feature: a controllable thinking budget (CoT length freely selectable, 512 tokens to unlimited); on hard tasks (AIME, LiveCodeBench) the score rises with a larger budget. Sampling follows the ByteDance recommendation temp=1.1 (!) / top_p=0.95 in chat; the high temperature is the vendor's intention; the coding profile is somewhat more conservative (temp 1.0 / top_p 0.8, compare Taubench 1.0/0.7). --jinja for the thinking template. Dense, so no MoE offload; quantised it fits well on a 32 GB card.
profile_notes.shieldstral.yaml: Mistral Shieldstral 1.0 3B is a policy-adaptive multimodal safety CLASSIFIER, not a conversational assistant. It is based on Ministral 3 and runs in current llama.cpp after Mistral-format conversion. Text moderation needs only the model GGUF; image moderation also needs the Pixtral mmproj. Use a single yes/no policy question per request. The client should request max_tokens=1 with logprobs/top_logprobs and derive the normalized yes/no score; that response-side setting is not a llama-server launch flag and therefore cannot be encoded in this YAML. Official inference uses greedy temperature 0.0. Although the base architecture exposes 256k RoPE, the model card recommends the 32k training range.
profile_notes.smollm3.yaml: HuggingFace SmolLM3-3B: dense 3B model, Apache-2.0, architecture "smollm3", dual-mode reasoning (think/no-think via /think or /no_think in the chat template), native 64k context (128k via YaRN). Sampling follows the HF card temp=0.6 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=40; coding slightly more deterministic. --jinja for template + reasoning separation. Small and fast; good as a draft model or for light edge workloads.
profile_notes.step35.yaml: StepFun Step 3.5 Flash (text) + Step 3.7 Flash (VLM, +image/video), both sparse MoE ~196-198B total / ~11B active, 3:1 SWA/full attention, MTP-3, 256k context. Both load under architecture "step35". SIZE WARNING: a ~196-198B MoE far exceeds this system's 48 GB (VRAM+RAM); realistically it runs only with massive CPU MoE offload and slow generation, or not at all. The profile exists for correctness/the future. Reasoning levels (low/medium/high) are controlled via the chat template/API. draft_max is set to 3 (native MTP-3 depth); possibly unstable on Vulkan, then reduce to 2 in the Expert panel. Step-3.7-Flash needs a separate mmproj file for vision. `--jinja` enables clean reasoning separation: -- --jinja
profile_notes.trinity-afmoe.yaml: Arcee AI Trinity (AFMoE / "afmoe", AfmoeForCausalLM): attention-first MoE, in llama.cpp since b7061. Nano = 6B total / ~1B active, Mini = 26B / ~3B, each with 128 experts (8 active, 1 shared), 128k native context. NOT a Mamba hybrid: full KV cache per layer (the tuner's hybrid logic correctly does NOT apply here). This profile also covers Dolphin-X1-Trinity-Nano (dphn), the RL-uncensored retrain of Trinity-Nano: same architecture, same ChatML template, only the alignment differs. With Dolphin the system prompt controls tone and alignment (for example "You are Dolphin, a helpful, unbiased, and uncensored AI assistant."); without a system prompt the model behaves in an unspecific default. Sampling follows Arcee's official recommendation (temp 0.15 / top_k 50 / top_p 0.75 / min_p 0.06), deliberately deterministic for stable tool/structured output. Trinity-Mini can run via vLLM with the deepseek_r1 reasoning parser + hermes tool parser; under llama.cpp `--jinja` handles the template/channel separation.
profile_notes.unlimited-ocr.yaml: OCR/document model. Use AutoTuner's OCR workflow so images are normalized, PDFs are rendered page-by-page, and Word/Office files are converted through LibreOffice before they are sent to llama-server. The verified prompt is "document parsing."; "Free OCR." can return immediate EOS on Unlimited-OCR.
profile_notes.vibethinker.yaml: WeiboAI VibeThinker: dense reasoning model (3B on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, or 1.5B), MIT licence, specialised in verifiable reasoning (maths/code/STEM). Architecture "qwen2", therefore NO arch_fallback (it would otherwise catch generic Qwen2 models); matching only by filename. Sampling follows the official WeiboAI recommendation temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=-1 in BOTH modes: a lower temperature demonstrably worsens reasoning quality here; the model is not trained for other temperature regimes. <think> block: parse downstream. Not a general-purpose model; take a larger model for broad world knowledge.
profile_notes.dfm-mimir.yaml: DFM Mimir is a 1B Danish/English instruction-tuned model from Danish Foundation Models on the HRM-Text (Hierarchical Reasoning Model) architecture: two 16-layer transformer stacks (low and high) run in alternating cycles (2 H-cycles x 3 L-cycles) over the same token stream, so every token passes 128 block slots built from 32 physical layers; hidden size 1,536, 12 attention heads without GQA, a 262,144-token vocabulary with a Gemma-4-style chat template, 4,096 native context, Apache 2.0. llama.cpp b11003 (PR #27625) added the hrm_text architecture; this profile requires that build. The KV cache holds one entry per pass (128 slots): about 3 GiB at 4,096 tokens in F16 and half of that with Q8 K/V, which AutoTuner sizes from the GGUF block_count; decode costs roughly four times a dense model of equal width. Upstream implements causal attention only, the prefix-LM mode of the reference is not available. DFM publishes no generation_config, so the sampling defaults are AutoTuner's generic values. The template needs --jinja; thinking is opt-in through enable_thinking.
profile_notes.dots-ocr.yaml: rednote-hilab dots.ocr: a 1.7B multilingual document parser on a Qwen2.5 language model (architecture qwen2) with a NaViT vision encoder. Sampling follows the reference parser (temp 0.1 / top_p 1.0, no top_k, no repetition penalty); a repetition penalty would damage tables and repeated characters. The published window is 32,768 tokens. Use the official task prompts such as "Extract the text content from this image." for plain OCR; layout prompts return JSON with bounding boxes. AutoTuner attaches a compatible sibling mmproj when present.
profile_notes.agnes-3_0-flash.yaml: Agnes-3.0-Flash Preview (Agnes AI, September 2026) is a 33B dense hybrid-attention multimodal reasoning model: 72 layers (54 gated delta-rule plus 18 global attention, 3:1), 262,144 native context, text, image and video input, tool calling, Apache-2.0. Its extra parallel SwiGLU branch has no mainline llama.cpp support, so community GGUFs either fold that branch into a standard qwen35 MLP (kingjones777, 0xKitkat, ngquocvinh; these load on any qwen35-capable mainline build) or keep it as ffn_*_par tensors (jakeatx, quimmedes; these need their patched forks). The kingjones777 MTP-ROCmFP4 / ROCmFPX files additionally use ROCmFPX tensor types (ggml types 100-111, file types 100-124) that only the ROCmFPX fork of llama.cpp loads (upstream PR #24185 is still open); AutoTuner refuses them before launch on any runtime whose llama library has no ROCmFP loader. Sampling follows generation_config (temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20); coding uses temp 0.6 like Qwen3.5. The in-file MTP head measured best at draft depth 4 with p-min 0 on the model card. The template accepts reasoning_effort xhigh (default), medium or low only, and preserve_thinking defaults to true. Measured on 2026-09-19 with the AutoTuner recipes (ROCmFPX main aed0d5fd9, fork build 11544, RDNA4 MMQ fallback patch): STRIX_LEAN decodes about 67 tok/s on HIP (R9700) and 29 tok/s on Vulkan with the MTP head, COHERENT matches it on HIP but drops to 5 tok/s on Vulkan (dual-scale ROCmFP4 shaders), and image requests succeed with the MTP head loaded on both backends, unlike the older fork build the model card measured.
profile_notes.ling-3_0-vl.yaml: InclusionAI Ling-3.0-flash-VL is the vision-language variant of Ling 3.0 Flash: the same 124B-A5.5B bailingmoe3 hybrid KDA/MLA MoE backbone plus a 27-block vision tower and projector for images and video. Pair it with its own mmproj file. llama.cpp b11156 (PR #29151) is required: it adds the ling3vl projector and M-RoPE; older builds load the text weights with plain rope and answer incorrectly, so AutoTuner refuses them. Thinking is on by default. Chat uses the generation config (temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20), coding the model card's evaluation default of temp 0.6. The native window is 131k; the 256k ceiling needs YaRN and is clamped to the GGUF metadata. Video input via the OpenAI video_url field needs b11136+ and is covered by b11156. Not tested locally (no weights installed).
profile_notes.kimi-k3_1.yaml: Moonshot Kimi K3.1 (Pro): a 2.8T-total/104B-active MoE (896 experts, 16 active, latent MoE) with 69 KDA layers and 24 gated-DSA attention layers, 1,048,576 tokens of context. Its kimi-k31 architecture needs llama.cpp b12180+ (PR #31779); the text model is supported, vision is not part of that PR. Reasoning effort is set per request (low, high, max; default max). Sampling from the model card: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95. This is a datacenter-scale model; local use needs aggressive quantization, large system RAM and CPU expert offload.
profile_notes.lfm3.yaml: LiquidAI LFM3 edge family (lfm3 architecture: short convolutions with sliding-window and global attention). LFM3-1.7B (262,144 tokens) and LFM3-VL-2B need llama.cpp b11938+ (PR #31252); LFM3-Audio-2B and LFM3-Omni-2B need b11941+ (PR #31257) for their audio projectors, video input arrived in b11960. Sampling from LiquidAI: temperature 0.1, top-k 50, repetition penalty 1.1 for chat, tools and coding (math and STEM: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20). Reasoning is on by default except for LFM3-Omni-2B, which does not think. The audio models answer as text in the chat server; speech output uses llama.cpp's audio paths. The d1 decision models of the family use the decision profile.
profile_notes.muse-spark-open.yaml: Muse Spark Open: an 816B-total/42B-active latent-space MoE (256 experts, 8 active) with text, image and audio input and up to 1,048,576 tokens of context (three sliding-window layers per global layer). Needs llama.cpp b11671+ (PR #30616); images use the Muse Glimmer vision tower, audio the muse-spark-audio projector. Sampling as stored in the ggml-org GGUFs: temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, top-k 64. Datacenter-scale: local use needs aggressive quantization, large system RAM and CPU expert offload.
profile_notes.mistral-large-4.yaml: Mistral Large 4: a roughly 1T-total/52B-active MoE with image input and a 1,048,576-token context window (mistral-large4 architecture, llama.cpp b11998+, PR #31376). Reasoning effort low, medium or high (default) is set per request. Sampling from Mistral's model card for every reasoning effort: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95. ggml-org publishes the GGUFs. Datacenter-scale: local use needs aggressive quantization, large system RAM and CPU expert offload.
profile_notes.clover.yaml: DiffuSpace Clover-35B-A3B-Preview: a block-diffusion language model on a Qwen3.6-MoE base (clover_moe architecture, 131,072 tokens). llama.cpp b12060+ (PR #31306) runs it in autoregressive mode only; the diffusion self-speculation is a separate upstream PR. Sampling from the shipped generation config: temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, presence penalty 0.9 and repetition penalty 1.05, which the authors set against repetition in long answers. Thinking is controlled through the chat template.
profile_notes.ripple.yaml: Ricursive Ripple-65B Preview: a dense 65B reasoning and agent model with up to 1,048,576 tokens of context (ricursive architecture, interleaved sliding-window and global attention). Needs llama.cpp b12158+ (PR #31692); the AtomicChat GGUFs carry the chat template with tools and thinking. The model card publishes no sampling settings, so the profile keeps llama.cpp's defaults (temperature 0.8, top-k 40, top-p 0.95, min-p 0.05).
profile_notes.limite.yaml: paradigma Limite 1B Violetto: a small mathematical reasoning model (limite architecture, llama.cpp b11988+, PR #29433). Its chat template requires the model's own fixed system prompt and rejects custom system messages, so leave the system prompt empty in clients. Sampling from the model card: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95. The profile caps the context at 32,768 tokens; the GGUF's own limit applies when it is lower.
profile_notes.flint.yaml: Recursive Flint: a 39.8B-total/2.5B-active MoE for coding agents (256 experts, 6 active plus a shared expert, sliding-window and full attention, 262,144 tokens). llama.cpp loads the flint architecture since b11803 (PR #30928); the hexadecimal string escapes its chat template needs came in b11798. Sampling from the model card: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, min-p 0.
profile_notes.minicpm-ocr-1_0.yaml: OpenBMB MiniCPM-OCR 1.0: a document OCR model on the MiniCPM-V 4.6 stack (qwen35 text model plus the minicpm_ocr_1_0 projector, llama.cpp b11826+, PR #30979). The model writes its transcription inside the thinking block, so the profile starts llama-server with --reasoning off and the text arrives in the normal content. Greedy decoding for transcription. The OpenBMB SDK sends cropped page regions; whole pages work but are slower. MiniCPM-OCR-Jev (the page/text decision scorer) uses the decision profile.
profile_notes.nemotron-3_5-transcribe.yaml: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe: an offline speech model (34B total with the audio encoder, 4.3B active) for transcription, translation and speaker attribution in 40 languages, recordings up to one hour, 65,536 tokens of context. Needs llama.cpp b12087+ (PR #31471) and its mmproj. The profile starts llama-server with --reasoning off and greedy decoding, as NVIDIA recommends for transcription; for audio understanding NVIDIA uses reasoning on with temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95. Word timestamps and streaming are not supported in llama.cpp yet.
profile_notes.nemotron-embed.yaml: NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Embed and Nemotron-3.5-Embed (1B and 8B) retrieval embedding models. NO chat: the profile starts an embedding endpoint (--embeddings, POST /v1/embeddings). Nemotron-3.5-Embed also embeds document page images through its mmproj; queries are text only. Prefix queries with "query:" and documents with "passage:" as the model card does. Needs llama.cpp b11833+ (conversion PR #30877 in b11778, Nemotron-3.5-Embed tokenizer fix PR #30974 in b11833). Context up to 32,768 tokens.
